description: Platform DOS Published by International PC Owners Released 1983 Genre Strategy/Tactics Perspective Top-down Description In Combots, two combat robots are put in an arena to see which can hit its opponent more times with a laser in the given time limit. To play the game, the player(s) program two combots by giving it ten commands. There are three commands the combots can perform: move, turn, or fire. The combots will repeatedly follow its commands in the arena until time runs out. (For example, you could program a combot to follow these instructions: move, fire, move, fire, turn, move, turn, fire, move, fire. The combot keeps performing these actions and you have to hope when it fires your opponent happens to be in the way at the time!) At the end of the time limit, whichever combot has more hits wins. The controls reflect this, with moving the controller to the right actually moving the character down and right, moving it down and right moving the character down directly, and so on. Each level is played out against a time limit, and the paths through the level aren’t always clear-cut. There are four different types of doors, each of which needs a particular icon to pass (the icons represent the door type, such as ice or bricks, rather than hot water or a key, or anything you’d logically expect to clear the path). You can avoid the baddies, which may be the best option, as killing them costs you some energy –this reduces the significance of the points system. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

description: Platform DOS Released 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Description Push Your Luck is a version of a classic dice game. Each round, you roll two dice as "blockers." Then roll five dice as long as you wish, getting the number of points each die shows. The catch is if you roll the same number as one of the blockers (it's possible, but unlikely, for both blockers to be the same number), you don't get points for that die and can no longer roll it. If you keep rolling until you roll all blockers, you get zero points for that round. You may stop at any time. There are a total of five rounds. The player with the highest total for the game wins. title: Attack of the Petscii Robots
description: It may appear that Attack of the Petscii Robots is an action game at first glance, but it's more of a strategic game with some action elements. The goal is to destroy all of the robots in the level. To do so, first you'll need to search around and find some weapons and items. Then you'll have to use them carefully in order to defeat all the baddies. It offers numerous graphic modes to choose from and some AdLib based music. It's a fun and charming game. Definitely a unique experience, although I personally found the constant "searching" mechanic to get a bit tiresome. This is a modern game created by David Murray (aka The 8-Bit Guy of YouTube fame) and ported to many systems; this DOS port is by Jim Wright. Note that the file is 16MB but most of that is the included PDF manual, which is really nicely done but is much, much larger than all of the game files put together! (You may want to read it if you want to learn how to play, you can view it online here.) If you like the game, buy the full version at the official 8-Bit Guy website, it comes in digital download plus a variety of physical release types if you're into that.

Aiming is complicated by the wind which blows from left or right with varying intensity, and by draft which deflects the arrows up or down. title: Final Impact
description: Final Impact is a game that possesses most of the qualities necessary for a hit game, with great production values, sound effects, and slick design. However, it unfortunately falls a bit short in the gameplay department. It's a mission-based shooting game with a similar format to Raptor, where you fly missions and earn money to buy new weapons and upgrades. The actual missions seem VERY difficult, and the way your ship fires (depending on the weapon, you can fire in 4 or 8 directions) is not easy to do. The default controls also probably will need to be reconfigured but thankfully you can do that within the game. Seems like a bit more playtesting would have made this game great, but as-is this demo is a great example of the kind of production values of this period of time. (Full game was released on CD with a full soundtrack.)

title: Black Hole
description: Black Hole is a timed puzzle game where the object is to clear all of the tiles off the screen by walking on them. According to its author Terry Cavanagh (yes, that one) it's based on a game called POD. The game is presented well and it seems like there are a lot of levels and a lot of variations on the basic gameplay which are gradually introduced as you play. The difficulty spikes up pretty rapidly with the fourth level already providing a decent challenge, especially since each level is also timed. Source code (QuickBasic) and a level editor are included. Consider buying Terry's excellent VVVVVV game and/or Terry's Other Games pack for more of his work.

title: Blupi at Home
description: Blupi at Home (the character is also sometimes referred to as Eggbert in English-speaking countries) is a game based around the French character Blupi. You use the mouse to click things around Blupi's house, and he will perform some action with them and also spell out the word for you to read. There are some minigames to discover as well. title: BLINDCHESS v.1.76
description: BlindChess for DOS is intended for blindfold chess training. But it can also be set to show the board. The program will also work under all Windows versions. If you own PocketDOS it will run on your palmtop device. It works finely on my Casio BE-300. You input moves at the command prompt by typing, e.g., 'g1f3'. Whenever you want you can display an ascii diagram of the board position. The program's response time depends only on the setting of search depth. On a modern computer, it replies instantaneously at 5 ply (that is, 5 ply minimum), which is the default setting. This can be changed with the command 'sd'. It is a minimax brute force program, with some positional intelligence, which is good enough for blindfold chess. The three-time repetition rule is not enforced, otherwise it's a fully adequate chess program. You can interrupt processing by typing any key. description: Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description PC-Fender is a Public Domain version of the classic Defender . When a level is completed the player moves on to the next and continues until either all levels have been played or they exhaust all their available lives. title: Kaboom
description: Kaboom is not a variant of the classic Atari 2600 game Kaboom. (If you're looking for that, try Kerboom! which is a decent DOS clone.) Anyways, this game is a deathmatch fighting game for up to four players. At least two human combatants are required, otherwise it'll be rather boring since there are no CPU opponents available. (This is apparently a public beta version so it's missing some features the author planned for the full game.) There are no weapons other than the default blaster, so you'll need to use that (and avoid all of the other things trying to kill you) to take out your opponents as you fly around the gritty industrial type arenas. It looks good and controls well, and there are plenty of options to tinker with, but the core gameplay won't likely hold your attention for too long, especially if you don't have a second player around to play with.

description: Chesshousers is an interesting and visually eye-catching puzzle game. The goal is to direct your player (a glove) through an isometic-perspective maze. You have no weapons, all you can do is move around and push/destroy certain objects. Chess pieces move as the do in the chess board game (ex, pawns move straight ahead) and you'll need to carefully think through their movement before you push them to progress. The graphics look great but the isometric viewpoint sometimes makes it unnecessarily difficult to see what's going on. title: Blam! Machinehead Demo (PC) (Corrected DOSBox Cycles)
description: Blam! Machinehead PC Demo (also for the Sega Saturn and Sony Playstation) featuring one level where you must destroy 10 cocoons, navigate the aqueduct turbines, restore power to the train generator, then follow it to the level exit. Collect green Unreality Keys (and one normal red key) to warp reality around you to progress through the level while hovering on a gun-totting self-destructing warhead! Keyboard controls can be rebound and is recommended to do so within the options. Ram into the Unreality Terminals at speed to use your Unreality Keys on them. While this game works better in local DosBox under Auto (browser version cannot seem to handle Core set to Auto, only Simple), it can be streamed in the browser version well enough. I have manually set Cycles to 71000, Prebuffer to 20, and audio Blocksize to 4096 to strike a balance between performance and audio skipping.

The tropes are familiar: royalty have lost valuable items and require their return, while exploration is thwarted with colour-coded locks -- can the player find or trade items for the quest objects and progress through the disjointed story via accessing more remote map areas? Instead of playing it straight with a poker face while mangling "thee"s and "thou"s, however, the author has strewn the game landscape with his high-school friends and titans of '90s industrial music. In the demo, the game ends after the fifth room, and in the completed version it ends at the tenth room of the fifth floor. Rules of the game: The rules are fairly straight forward. So in this "virtual reality" game (created using the Virtual Reality Studio software) you run (or slowly stumble your way through) a simulated 3D-ish environment and click on things to try to get to the next area. Like most Virtual Reality Studio engine games, it's a bit awkward to navigate around, and knowing what to do takes a lot of trial and error. It is a shareware game that showcases what ZZT can do. Epic MegaGames created ZZT with its game worlds and released it together with its level editor and world creation tools. This proved hugely popular and led to many home made worlds being created and shared on-line via bulletin boards. In 1991 Epic held a Game Design Contest to find the best of these game boards and they received over one thousand entries. Game boards from this contest were used to create two new game worlds, 'The Secret of Headhunter Isle' and 'Royal Treasures' which Epic released as shareware in 1992 under the name Best of ZZT . title: bef v2.11 (Befunge-93 interpreter) for DOS
description: Befunge-93 is an esoteric programming language where programs are assemblages of characters arranged in a two-dimensional, Cartesian grid. bef is the reference interpreter for the Befunge-93 language. This Internet Archive item runs bef version 2.11, built for DOS using Borland C++ 3.1, running under DOSBox. It also includes the Befunge-93 example programs from that time. A menu system is included to help demonstrate the language, as well as a simple text editor (TED3.COM) to allow the user to modify or create new Befunge-93 programs. Note that bef 's debug mode uses the DOS blinking underline cursor to indicate the current execution position in the program, but DOSBox does not emulate this well; if the cursor is moving rapidly it simply does not display it. The goal is simple: choose the traits of Moppet creatures to line up in a queue, obeying the given number of rules. For instance, if the rule says "2," you must choose the traits of the next Moppet so that it differs from the previous Moppet by 2 traits, e.g. a fat, blue Moppet can stand next to a thin, red Moppet. The number of rules, i.e. traits, can be changed from 1 to 4, thus either making the game more or less challenging (although changing the traits to 4, the maximum, will just result in your Moppets being an alternate sequence of two types of Moppets). title: Bugs!
description: Platform DOS Released 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Top-down Description Bugs! is a free, text-mode clone of Centipede written in Pascal (some versions include the source). A horde of insects is invading, and the only cure is an inexhaustible supply of ASCII arrows, fired from a gun that can be moved throughout a narrow band at the bottom of the playfield. An assortment of nasty bugs infests the mushroom-littered field: the segmented centipede, which descends from the top, and whose path depends on the placement of mushrooms; the spider, bouncing along the bottom and consuming the scattered fungi; the flea, which drops by to deposit new growths; and the scorpion, which poisons any mushroom in its path. The game is intended to be authentic to the sport of drag racing and like the real thing times the races to 1/1000 of a second. title: EdChess
description: EdChess (later re-published as commercial software under the more generic and enthusiastic name Chess!) is a computer chess program in text-mode. It allows play of two human players, play against the CPU, or watching a CPU vs CPU match. The pieces are represented crudely with 3x3 or 3x2 ASCII boxes. You can change the ability of the CPU by modifying the "difficulty" (maximum thinking time for the computer) and "think ahead" (whether the CPU can be processing while you're making your move). You can also review the moves made by going forward or backward. Overall it's a fairly basic but competent chess program.

title: Operation Cleaner
description: Platform DOS Released Jun 14, 1998 Genre Simulation, Strategy/Tactics Pacing Turn-based Gameplay Platform Description Operation Cleaner is a Finnish freeware game exploring a very unique genre of gaming: demolition of buildings. The player is in charge of a demolition company, and the goal is to bring down buildings of the clients with as little explosives and collateral damage as possible. For simplicity and due to the age of the game the buildings are represented as 2D cross sections with all the bearing structures clearly visible. Player has to place various type of explosives into the buildings with a minimal amount of detonation wire and blast caps used. The nearby structures are protected with dampers. Although the physics engine is very simple and has some obvious flaws that lead to physically impossible situations at times, the game is very versatile as there often isn't one clear way of detonating a building in an optimal way. description: Also For Amiga, Atari ST, Commodore 64 Published by Software 2000 Released 1991 Genre Puzzle Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Shiftrix is a puzzle game with similarities to Atomix . The player is presented with a top-down level with differently coloured blocks. Those blocks can be moved in any direction, but they automatically move into the chosen direction until they meet an obstacle, e.g. a wall or another block. In contrast to Atomix , the goal is not to create a shape but to vaporize all blocks with the usual tile-matching method: two or more blocks of the same colour disappear when they touch. Each level has to be solved within a certain time frame and a limited amount of bombs can be used to kill off single blocks. description: Platform DOS Released 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description In this simple shooter, a city faces off against a never-ending succession of alien saucers that seem to have taken an interest in flying over its curiously-geometric skyline. There's only a single gun to shoot them down with, and it is necessary to lead the target based on its varying altitude and velocity. The UFOs themselves do not seem to mean any harm to the angular architecture below, and stoically attempt to gain passage without ever fighting back, so why they're being picked on is an open question. It is possible to control the ball's course somewhat by bouncing it off different sections of the paddle. If all three balls fall through the bottom of the screen (without being deflected by the paddle), it's game over; if you manage to tear the walls down completely, you'll be awarded the prestigious title of "wallbanger" - only to start again with zero points, since the game ends after a single level. The bell tower of Notre Dame Cathedral is one of the most famous sights in all of Paris and home to the most magical and heartwarming stories ever told... Journey back to medieval Paris and relive the amazing adventure of kind hearted Quasimodo, whom the frightened people call the Hunchback of Notre Dame. This CD-ROM includes full-length video, an animated storybook and games for the computer!

At that time in the Earth's history a terrible plague known as the Nagroma, swept the land at the start of winter killing every living thing it encountered. With the aid of the Inovar the Eharin were able to create a protective barrier that kept the plague at bay. In this game the player controls a star ship and must navigate through a hyper maze. The player starts in the bottom right hand corner of the maze and must navigate through to a gap in the game's border that's over in the top left corner. The ship is controlled by the numeric keypad and can move up / down, left / right. The maze is very congested and it is hard to find a way through. Fortunately the ship has a supply of missiles with which the obstacles can be removed. Unfortunately new obstacles appear at random around the screen so a clear path can sometimes become blocked. title: Eliminator
description: Eliminator is a Snake / Nibbles / Tron lightcycles clone. Your job is to survive and avoid crashing into walls while your snake gets longer, as your opponent attempts to do the same. This game provides a two-player mode as well as a single player mode against a quite difficult computer opponent. CGA graphics are used and no sound effects. There are no options beyond the aforementioned settings besides setting the speed, but on modern computers you'll need to turn the speed way down to make this game playable.

description: Keith Van Eron's Pro Soccer Also For Amiga, Amstrad CPC, Atari ST, Commodore 64, ZX Spectrum Developed by Sensible Software Published by Microplay Software Released 1989 Genre Sports Perspective Top-down Sport Football (European) / Soccer Misc Licensed Description Arcade-style soccer game. It has two different parts: Indoor and Outdoor. The Outdoor game is the normal European soccer. You may play single matches, league or tournament (world championships). Optional features are: weather effects, replays, customizable game length. Some quite funny movements and shots are available (e.g. banana flanks). The Indoor game has US soccer teams (?fictional?) and plays on a much smaller field. It has different rules compared to outdoor soccer. You can play single matches, league and All Star tournament. The same movements and shots can be made, sometimes with even funnier effects (e.g. banana shot bouncing of the wall and into goal). From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Power Grand Prix
description: Power Grand Prix is a car racing game, which was programmed in 1996 for MS-DOS. The player can play alone against the computer or together with a second player. If he plays alone, he takes part in the Grand Prix circuit where he competes against a computer opponent on different race tracks. If he beats the computer in all races, he becomes the new world champion and receives world cup. The first player controls his race car with the arrow keys and accelerates and stops it with the A key. The second player controls his race car completely with the joystick or a joypad.

title: Field General
description: Developed by rbm software Platform DOS Released Jan 15, 1992 Genre Sports Pacing Turn-based Sport Football (American) Description Field General is an American Pro Football game for one or two players. The game is entirely keyboard controlled. The player(s) name their teams and can either direct all elements of the play themselves or they can opt to have the teams play automatically. This game is not a management game, there's no player's draft, no financial juggling, none of that sort of stuff. The key, and allegedly unique, feature of this game is that both teams start off equal and it is the player(s) ability in calling the plays that decides who is victorious. From Mobygames.com. title: Operation Combat
description: Published by Merit Software Released 1990 Also For Amiga Genre Strategy Perspective 3rd-Person Perspective Theme Turn-based Description Operation Com0MBat is a basic, turn-based strategy game. Two armies stand against each other on a battlefield with the goal to destroy the enemy headquarters. With the help of a overhead map and statistics for each vehicle, players plan their moves for each turn: moving a vehicle within a certain radius and then choosing a target to fire at. Additionally there is also a powerful air strike available which uses up a whole turn. The map can be a combination between three scenarios (change what vehicles are used) and six battlefields. There are also various options for changing the game settings, e.g. the time limit of a turn or the firing behaviour of the units. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

The hero's default gun with unlimited ammunition can be exchanged for stronger ones (but with limited ammo) by picking a correspondent power-up. Other power-ups include shields that further protect the hero from attacks, dynamite, and health-restoring items. A boss battle awaits Van Slug at the end of each stage. title: Wall Pipe
description: Developed by Soleau Software, Inc. Platform DOS Published by Soleau Software, Inc. Released 1993 Genre Puzzle Pacing Real-Time Perspective Top-down Interface Point and Select Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Wall Pipe is a real-time puzzle game where you need to lead flowing water through a series of pipes. On each screen is a water source, and a number of pipe parts queued up for you to build the pipeline with, by picking the first pipe-part in the queue, using your mouse, and placing it where you want. Some planning ahead is possible, as the next three queued parts are visible. There is a 40 second delay after the level starts until the water flows, during which time you can try to build the longest pipe from the available parts. It is not possible to turn the parts around to fit the connection, unlike e.g. Tetris , nor can you see the part you have in your hand, so you must remember the shape, once it's removed from the queue. title: Vampiric Tower
description: Platform DOS Released 2000 Genre Adventure Gameplay Puzzle elements Perspective Top-down Description The player controls a comely purple-haired lady vampire, collecting vials of blood through fifty rooms (ten per level). A given room can't be traversed until all the blood is collected, the portcullis opening to the next chamber. The path ahead and upward is not without obstacles however -- the rooms are filled with pushable blocks (get it out of your way -- but not into a place where it will obstruct access to the blood!), spikes that can't be walked on, as well as numerous spooky enemies whose unimpeded line-of-sight gaze is lethal. To help in traversing some of these hazards, as a vampire the player has a limited amount of transformations at their disposal -- the bat can fly over the spikes and around urns, but has to return to human form in order to collect the vials. As the game was further developed, numerous changes and additions compared to the original were introduced, including but not limited to: A wilderness with multiple towns. description: Developed by EK Corporation Platform DOS Released Sep 15, 1995 Genre Adventure Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure Perspective 1st-person Description Like VariTale before it, TEA is a BBS door for automating the infrastructure permitting the playing of Choose-Your-Own-Adventure type plot-forking games -- all it needs are the stories, provided by your BBS userbase (or, optionally, by an included sample pack of 65 rooms)! title: Four Card Solitaire
description: Platform DOS Published by Softdisk Publishing Released Feb, 1989 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Cards / Tiles Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description In this solitaire game, the player has four columns to work with, and each starts with just one card in it. Whenever two cards on the bottoms of stacks have the same suit, the card with the lowest value can be removed. At any time, a single card may also be moved from the bottom of any stack to a vacant column or a new set of four cards may be dealt onto the bottoms of the stacks. The object of the game is to have an ace at the top of every column. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Janosik
description: Also For Amiga Published by Mirage Software Released Jun 23, 1994 Genre Action Gameplay Platform Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Janosik is an enhanced port of Atari game of the same title . Graphics and audio aspects were adapted to the 16-bit computers, boards entirely remodeled. The game introduced some new elements, like animated short scenes or new types of obstacles. The game world is divided into forest, village and castle areas. Armed with a shepherd's axe and precise jumping ability Janosik must defeat all the enemies to free Maryna. This platform game is loosely based on the story around Juraj Jánošík, a XVII / XVIIIc. Slovak highlander, leader of Carpathian brigands. In Poland the legend was revived by a popular TV series from 1970s, making him a fictional XIXc. gallant folk hero, who only robs the rich Austrian nobles to help oppressed local peasants, "Robin Hood way". From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Road Rally
description: Platforms DOS, TRS-80 Published by Adventure International Released 1979 Genre Racing / Driving Pacing Turn-based Description Somewhat unusually for a driving game, Road Rally is presented entirely in a turn-based, textual format. Your goal is to drive a 5-mile distance from home to the Old Mill Stream. There are five courses, ranging from relatively straight to riddled with curves, and you have a choice of four vehicles: a Volkswagen, a Chevy, a Mazda RX-7, and a Ferrari. Trouble is, you only have half a gallon in your tank... and the faster the car, the more gas it will guzzle. A game turn represents 10 seconds of driving time, and gives you a run-down of your current stats and road conditions. On each turn, you get the option to adjust your gas rate, by entering a number from -10 (hard braking) to 10 (hard acceleration): this is the only form of control you have over your car. Careful speed control is required in order to avoid crashing, navigate curves safely, keep your engine…

The game employs 3 different camera angles to capture the most realistic aspect on the course. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Caddiehack CGA Tour
description: This is Caddiehack CGA Tour, a 1989 game that mobygames calls Caddiehack Golf (1988) a sequel to. Either someone's very wrong, or the creators at Micode Developments had access to a very useless time machine. This is the free demo version. Feature-wise it seems to be very similar to Caddiehack Golf, just aimed at CGA systems instead of EGA/VGA. It has a lovely color scheme, thanks to using the Cyan/Magenta/Light Gray of CGA Mode 4/Palette 1/Low Intensity, with the normally-black background redefined to be green. Very Aesthetic, which is how I first learned of this game . Anyway the EGA/VGA version was already up on the internet archive, but not this version. So I'm fixing that.

The game has all the standard features that would be expected, automatic save state on exit, a short game mode as well as a super short game mode, and a time limit function. The game also has a speed control which allows the player(s) to adjust the time the on-screen messages are displayed thus potentially making the game faster. Unusually it also has a demo mode and a pitch control that adjusts the frequency of the sound the dice make when rolling. They move left or right and at random points they erect ladders to scale the castle walls and they can also shoot arrows. title: Tristam Island (MS-DOS)
description: After crashing your plane at sea, you end up drifting to a small island, with not much to survive. You explore, and find out the island was inhabited, years ago. But why did the people leave? And why is there a fence around the white house at the top of the hill? TRISTAM ISLAND is a text adventure made from the mold of Infocom; expect a large geography to explore, lots of prose, a rich parser, diverse puzzles, some humor and some darkness. To use Infocom's classification, I'd rate the game's difficulty as "Standard"; however, the game's design is modern and eschews all the frustrations commonly associated with 1980s text adventures. No hunger timers, no frustrating mazes, no blocking situations that force you to restart.

title: Windoze
description: Windoze Platform DOS Released Oct 03, 1994 Genre Puzzle Pacing Real-Time Gameplay Falling Block Puzzle Description Windoze is a variation on Columns which pokes fun at Microsoft's popular operating system, as evidenced by its use of the fashionable Usenet epithet for that OS at the time. The familiar colored blocks are replaced with various icons from Windows 3.x, which descend from above in groups of three and pile down at the bottom. The triplets can be moved, flipped and rotated as they fall, and points are scored by forming rows, columns or diagonals of 3 or more identical icons, thus removing them from the pile. The action speeds up as it goes on, and every 1000 points a special "wildcard" block appears: touch it down on an icon, and its matching brethren will all be wiped out in one fell swoop. title: SDI - Strategic Defense Initiative
description: Platform DOS Released 1988 Genre Action Gameplay Shooter Perspective 3rd-person (Other), Top-down Setting Cold War Description Not to be confused with similarly-named games (like the Cinemaware title or the Sega/Activision one ), SDI is a shooter in the vein of Missile Command . The player controls a single American SDI satellite, and must protect the USA from a succession of Soviet attack waves, by zapping incoming missiles before the nuclear warheads connect with their targets. The action is viewed from orbit, as enemy missiles are launched from multiple locations (including a bomber, which may be destroyed); they target population centers, military installations, and the satellite itself. After each wave, a score bonus is awarded for cities saved, and a penalty for cities destroyed. The number of surviving missile bases affects the USA's ability to retaliate, and the player's performance will determine the post-war scenario. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

You build your own 'Rube Goldberg' machine. Build your machine from an assortment of parts. Launch the ball into your machine. Points are scored as the ball interacts with your machine. title: Mad Mix Game (DOS)
description: Mad Mix is a Pac-Man variant, with a typical bird's eye view for each level and pellets you must eat in order to get to the next stages. Navigate the maze you're trapped in and gobble up food while trying to avoid the ghosts that are chasing you. As a Pac-Man variant, there are some changes made to distinguish itself. Some levels offer transformative powers. These include being turned into a hippopotamus - which allows you to step on ghosts - and a vacuum cleaner - to clean up pellets corrupted by a wandering enemy. On some levels, you can also briefly turn the protagonist into a spaceship or a tank, where you can shoot ghosts from a fixed vantage point. As with most arcade titles at the time, there is no true ending; the game loops back to the first level when you finish the last one. (Description from MobyGames ) Default controls: Left: O Right: P Up: Q Down: A Fire: Space Pause: H Keys can be redefined by selecting 2 in the main menu.

Released Mar, 1988 Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Sport Tennis Genre Action, Sports Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Hover is a futuristic Tennis-like game for two players. Each controls a racket-wielding character on one side of the court, and gains points by sending the ball flying past the other player and into the opposing wall. Ball movement is determined by the physics of gravity and momentum; both players are also equipped with a jetpack, which can be activated for some Y-axis action. Your task is to escape from the Asylum using the objects you find to solve the problems. Along the way though you will encounter the other inmates. The game is a graphical text adventure. The screen is split into two halves. The top half shows what you can see in front of you, in the bottom is the text describing your surroundings: here you can type commands. Using the arrow keys you move yourself about a 3D maze. You can draw a map. since it is easy to get lost. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Some diamonds are easy to get, but others require using dynamite sticks, given at the start of the level, to blast walls. To use dynamite, you press a letter on your keyboard to show which direction the blast should be aimed to. When you run out of time, you have an opportunity to see the whole maze and find what you missed. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Following the Lamers premise of AI-controlled Lemming-like Lamers (here dressed in Santa suits) securing their own safe passage through a hostile landscape toward a computer for them to muck up, the task before the player is to use all tools available to thwart them. With more seasonal hazards to employ than the conventional arms featured in its predecessor, here the player deploys limited amounts of Christmas toys and cruel factors of the winter weather -- snowballs and buckets of ice water. Will nothing drive away these Lamers? From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Like in Super Mario Bros you get bonus items by bouncing on floating blocks, such as invulnerability or extra lives. None of them are power-ups, this means every enemy contact results in a life loss. The player controls the titular character as he runs through labyrinths, trying to reach the exit before the time allotted for the stage completion runs out. Combat is action-based, with free movement and attacking; the players needs to move a cursor with the arrow keys to aim and shoot. The hero is equipped with various firearms, most of which require ammunition, while others need batteries to function. Batteries also power-up the protagonist's armor and the radar that displays a mini-map of the stage, and must be found and collected regularly. The hero can also cast spells, which work like expendable items. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

description: Do-Whacka-Do Released : 1993 Size : 158 KB Programming : White Shadow Requirements : 386 Intel VGA Graphics Adapter Option for sound : 100% Soundblaster Compatible Compatibility : MS-DOS Based Another processor and graphics intensive demo with a LOT of action going on the screen. -- Available for your viewing pleasure, intros by White Shadow . These 'hacks' contain some of the purest technical tricks to push the IBM-PC to its limits. Well, maybe back in the day when they were made to run at frame-rate on a 286. With the brute-force available in a Pentium and above, the same results can be had using any lame routine in any language, even COBOL. (: But as the tradition of demo coding has changed from hacking the hardware for doing things it shouldn't to full movie-productions, these demos remain true to the old C64 and Atari-ST scene of demo-making. In that sense, these demos deserve more credit than they probably get. True hardware hacking like this isn't easy to come by. We have no…

title: Rocket
description: Platform DOS Released Dec, 1981 Genre Action, Simulation Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description The Apollo lunar lander had just entered orbit at an altitude of 120 miles above the surface of the moon, when its computer decided to fail catastrophically. You take manual control of the capsule, and your job (as in most Lunar Lander games ) is to land it safely on the surface. In this case, your only control is over the fuel burn rate, which determines the upward thrust necessary to counter gravity and to help the capsule land in one piece. Burn rate must be carefully adjusted in real time, while keeping an eye on current altitude, velocity, weight and remaining fuel. The physics are recalculated once per second, and the lander's final impact velocity determines your success: 1.2 MPH or less is a perfect landing; more than 60 MPH will blast a new lunar crater (and get you deservedly chewed out for killing the crew). From…

description: from the textris.doc file: Textris is a twist on the familiar Tetris game. Rather than blocks of varying shapes, it has falling letters from which you can make words. Words must be from 3-7 letters long, and must not be capitalized names or trademarks. EGA or better. This is from Chapter 4 of the Fatal Distractions CD .

title: Usurper, The - The Mines Of Qyntarr
description: Also For Apple II Published by Sir-tech Software, Inc. Released 1989 Genre Adventure Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure, Puzzle elements Setting Fantasy Description The player is in a dark forest. The only hint is a placard nailed to a tree, with a warning: anyone seeking the Orb will meet a fitting end, signed King Aken by his Lord Lieutenant K'vin. Further exploration reveals a stone pedestal, a log cabin, and a dark cave. Exploring the cave without a light source will result in certain death by a yallou . It's up to the player to figure out how to proceed. Book One of The Usurper: The Mines Of Qyntárr (in-game title) is a text adventure game with a fantasy setting. The game tracks how many moves the player makes and will award the player points (out of 500) for progress in the game. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

description: Platforms Amiga, DOS Developed by Audiogenic Software Ltd. Published by Audiogenic Software Ltd. Released 1995 Genre Action, Sports Perspective Bird's-eye view Sport Cricket Description Cricket internationals are known as 'test' matches, but to many English and Australian players, most games are a mere test of ability to play in the Ashes, the fabled tours between the 2 countries taking place roughly every 18 months. title: Spryjinx
description: Platform DOS Released Dec, 1997 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform Description Spryjinx is a platform game in which two players compete to get the highest score by jumping on platforms. Platforms are moving from the top of the screen to the bottom where they are destroyed. Initially all the platforms are grey but when a player jumps onto a platform it will change color to that players color. A number on the platform indicates how much points it is worth and this amount will be added to the players score when it drops out of the screen. In addition to standard platform blocks with numbers on them there are ones with a question mark (gives a random number of points) and ones with a red devil (moves to adjacent free spaces). To make the game more interesting there are several bonus items: Paint bucket: Allows the player to paint platform blocks permanently. The opponent can not change the color. title: Tommy's Palace
description: Developed by Tommy's Toys Platform DOS Published by Tommy's Toys Released 1986 Genre Action, Strategy/Tactics Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Fantasy Description Tommy's Palace is a single player action / strategy game in which the player attempts to storm a castle. The player is the leader of a raid on the palace of 'The Dragon King'. The player is a blue character and all soldiers on his side are white. The enemy are coloured. To complete the game the player must fight through the eight floors of the palace to the throne room. Each room contains a trap door which can end the player's turn or lead to other rooms. In addition there are stairways which lead to the next level and once a room has been cleared the player uses the stairway to progress. The game is controlled using function keys and the numeric keypad From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Czorian Siege
description: Developed by Computer Applications Unlimited Platform PC Booter Published by Howard W. Sams & Co., Inc. Released 1983 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Czorian Siege is an arcade action game similar to Space Invaders . You control a spaceship at the bottom of the screen and need to defend yourself from the waves of attacking enemies. Each time you clear the screen of all enemies, you move on to the next, more difficult round. Each round also has a time limit; if the time limit expires but you still haven't destroyed all of the enemies, you will move on to the next round anyway. There are eight different types of enemy ships that will appear, plus on many of the screens there is a shield which you will need to shoot through before you can hit the various ships. You begin the game with four lives, and additional lives can be earned for every 5,000 points. The game ends when you have lost all of…

title: Last Half of Darkness III
description: Last Half of Darkness III Developed by SoftLab Laboratories Platform DOS Published by SoftLab Laboratories Released 1993 Genre Adventure Perspective 1st-person Narrative Horror Description The sequel to Last Half of Darkness Part II starts where Part II left off. The hero finds himself stranded alone on an island inhabited by living dead (which seem to not have vicious or violent intentions) and, again, has to find the girl he saved in the previous chapters of the saga. The third installment of the series utilizes a different engine and interface. Instead of selecting concrete verb commands, the players interacts with the environment in a point-and-click fashion. Another difference is the introduction of a life bar for the player character, which reduces the amount of instant death moments, replacing them with damage taken by the protagonist. The exploration is also more open-ended than in the previous installments. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

You should explore 80 rooms, walking from one room to another. Each room has one entrance and one exit, and it is filled with mechanical enemies and different useful mechanisms such as elevators, teleports, directional platforms, etc. You should move in four directions to avoid the enemies, or you may shoot them to break them for some period of time. One of 5 kinds of combining suits and helmets are available in certain rooms to increase your health energy, which may be decreased by collision with enemies. The highest score will be saved. title: Bomber Boy
description: Developed by vIRTUAL tECHNOLOGIES Platform DOS Released 1995 Genre Strategy/Tactics Perspective Top-down Description Bomber Boy is a game for two, three or four players and it is entirely keyboard controlled. Games are played over one, two, three or four matches. The game is a variant of the game Bomberman but without the storyline. Players start in opposite corners of a game area and place bombs to blow up the bricks that obstruct their passage, but running away before they detonate. The blast from each explosion clears one or more blocks and occasionally uncovers a bonus item. The objective of the game is to clear a path through to one's opponents and catch them in a blast thus killing them. Players have three lives and can only lay one bomb at a time. There were ten levels in the shareware version which has no single player option and no computer controlled opponents. However the full game promises thirty five levels, seven worlds, two computer opponents and Com2Com support From…

title: Chess Housers
description: Developed by Diabolic Soft Platform DOS Published by Digital Dreams Multimedia Released 1993 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Chess Perspective Top-down Interface Direct Control Visual Isometric Description Chess Housers is a puzzle game from Spain. The player guides a disembodied glove with the ARROW keys through a isometric labyrinth with a checkerboard pattern on the floor and lots of chess pieces placed. The glove has to push ( ARROW keys + SPACE bar) this pieces to clear its way to the exit. The pieces move with the same pattern that they have on chess: pawns move forward, horses have an "L"-shaped movement, and so on. The glove can be killed if it is in their path. The chess pieces are set up in small rooms as a series puzzles that must be solved. Other objects in the rooms include: ► Boulders that must be smashed by the horse pieces, if they're in the way; ► Transparent boxes , usually found stopping the movement of a piece, that can be destroyed by the glove; ► Pyramid teleporters to…

title: RAMSAK
description: Platform DOS Published by Heigen Corporation Released 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description RAMSAK is a game similar to Pac-Man , but completely rendered in ASCII art. The player (a white smiling face) travels on a field, trying to collect all dots and symbols and escaping evil Red Faces. There are also destructible (light-blue) and indestructible (dark blue) blocks on field. There is only one playing field, but it is randomly generated: there is random block placement, in-field bonus symbols randomly restocked after each death, and, moreover, each Red Face can remove or place any symbol on board (including indestructible blocks). There are no different levels and the game plays on the same board until the player loses all lives. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Game Builder Lite
description: A system that supposedly allows you to create your own Sierra-like adventure game. However, although it features EGA graphics, walk-behinds, etc. I found the system to be limiting in many ways (besides the fact that it allows you to create only adventure games) and that it wasn't easy or intuitive to use. Check it out, but be wary ... AGS (Adventure Game Studio) is probably a more robust and overall better choice. (Note that this download is now actually for the full version, Game Builder Pro, which was released for free by MVP Software.)

title: Chess and Checkers
description: Platform DOS Released 1988 Pacing Turn-based Perspective Top-down Genre Strategy/Tactics Interface Point and Select Gameplay Board Game, Chess Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Chess & Checkers is a simple, two player, shareware implementation of these classic board games. There is no 'intelligence' in this game, it is not possible to play against the computer, the game merely presents an electronic board on which two players can play each other. It is entirely keyboard controlled. The player uses the arrow keys to target a piece and presses the spacebar to select it. They then use the arrow keys to select the destination square and the ENTER key to move the piece to it. There is no save game function, no sound effects, and no game configuration options From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Rush Hour
description: Platform DOS Released Sep, 1987 Genre Simulation Pacing Real-Time Perspective Top-down Gameplay Managerial / Business Simulation Description A traffic control simulation in which the player must manage the flow of vehicles throughout a busy city block, during the rush hours of 7:00-9:00 AM. Every car has a particular destination, and as the clock ticks, traffic density increases and the streets jam up. Score is determined by the number of waiting cars during each game minute (the lower, the better). Each traffic light may be toggled individually or using an automated control system. After 7:40, all unlit lights come on automatically; at 8:00 the automated system fails - the lights must be controlled manually, and cannot be turned off until 8:46. The simulation ends at 9:00, and success is determined by the number of waiting (and total) cars at that point; if too many cars line up at any of the entry points during the game, the player loses. It is possible to redirect traffic between…

title: TurboGo
description: TurboGo Also For Windows Released Feb 28, 1993 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Perspective Top-down Description TurboGo is a computer version of the two-player Chinese board game weiqi ("Go") using the Chinese scoring rules. In this version of the game, either player can be a computer or human. The available board sizes here are 9x9, 13x13 and 19x19, the latter being a common tournament size grid. The Go game is simple, but hard to master, and this version has an extensive manual built into it to help. The two players have either black or white stones, and place them in turn on the cross-points of a square line grid. The object is to encircle/border off territory and capture the opponents stones as prisoners. The game can be saved to disk, and be continued later, as the larger boards can take some time to finish. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: CityRunner
description: Platform DOS Released 1995 Genre Action, Racing / Driving Gameplay Arcade Perspective 3rd-person (Other) Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description CityRunner is a futuristic search-and-rescue driving game featuring a 3D voxel-based environment, all in 4KB (!) of executable size. The player sits behind the wheel of a polygonal police car (shuttle? hovercraft?) and gets to zoom along the city streets in search of trouble hotspots, indicated by flashing buildings, which must be located and bumped against to rescue the distressed citizens therein. The objective is to save as many targets as quickly as possible, without running out of time or crashing the vehicle in the process. Each assignment starts at the station, with a time limit, a set number of targets, and full shields to protect the car against impact. title: Pixel Puzzler
description: Developed by Softdisk Publishing Platform DOS Published by Softdisk Publishing Released Feb, 1990 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Cards / Tiles Description This program takes graphic files, splits them into squares and shuffles the squares around. By selecting two squares with the keyboard or mouse, the player can swap their locations on the screen. The object is to reassemble the image to its original appearance. A variety of now-obscure graphics formats are supported: *.PIC, *.SCN, *.BSP, *.BSS, *.PAK, *.PBL, *.IFF and *.LBM. The puzzles can scale from 32 to 256 pieces in size. It is possible to save and later reload a puzzle in progress. The program also comes with Pixel Puzzle Maker, a utility which allows Print Shop clip art to be used to create new *.BSP graphics for use in the Puzzler. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Koach Tzabar
description: Developed by pmd Platform DOS Published by Tzabar Released 1997 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Puzzle elements Perspective Top-down Description Koach Tzabar is a promotional game distributed along with the Israeli Tzabar Salads. The gameplay is similar to Xonix . The player needs to reveal 9 lids of Tzabar Salads by "occupation areas", and be careful from the enemies. A life is lost when there is contact with an enemy. The player needs to "occupy" the percentage that appears on the right side in order to go to the next level. The game contains three levels of difficulty. In the easy difficulty the game does not have a time limit, unlike the advanced and professional difficulty levels. In the latter two if the player does not occupy the required percentage in time, a life is lost. The game also contains bonuses that help the player (move faster, the little enemies will explode, pause all the enemies for 5 seconds and more). From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Spinout
description: Platform DOS Released Jan, 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Paddle / Pong Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Spinout is a clone of the game Breakout and features similar gameplay. At the top of the screen are four rows of bricks; the goal is to remove all of the bricks by hitting them with a bouncing ball. The player controls a paddle at the bottom of the screen which is used to deflect the ball. The game begins with five balls, and if a ball makes it past the paddle it is lost. The game ends when all bricks are successfully destroyed or all five balls are lost. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

description: Platform DOS Released Jul, 1993 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling Description A jail break has occurred in the city of Megatropolis and five evil supervillains have escaped. The city's last resort is to summon a team of superheroes, each with their own strengths, weaknesses, and special abilities. The gameplay is similar to the Apogee EGA titles, like Duke Nukem and Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure: Forbidden Planet . There is a grand total of 50 levels to play and 7 characters to choose from. description: Platform DOS Released 1983 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Description Ario Bros is a single player, platform game that uses character graphics. In this game the player has to keep the plumbing free of pests while collecting points. To collect the pest the player jumps up and bangs the platform beneath the pest, this temporarily stuns them so that they can be collected. Collected pests leave behind coins which score points. Some pests can be stunned with just one jump, others take two or more. The game also has a POW box. When hit this stuns all pests but its effect is reduced with repeated use. There's a fireball bouncing around the screen, if the player catches it they will score highly on the other hand if the fireball hits the player it's game over. Choose your vehicle and enter the arena to face your computer opponents to see who scores the most goals before the clock runs out. Scoring isn't easy. The ball constantly bounces over the arena, retrieved by a player constantly bombarded by opponents. A variety of weapons are available to shoot your competitor, and anyone that takes a hit while carrying the ball loses possession, sending the ball bouncing across the arena. You must remotely pilot an unarmed science robot to explore the ship and work out how to shut the weapon down. The game uses interactive quarter-screen footage to display the ship's interiors. The main challenge is that an automated security device is chasing you down, and must be avoided and ultimately destroyed. A delay between your commands and the robot's receipt of them forces you to pay close attention to the security drone and plan several steps ahead. As you explore the ship, you will find data ports, which can be jacked into to gain information or to open doorways. To access most of these, you will need to find and collect a DNA sample from a member of staff whose role gave him/her access.

This can be achieved by avoiding two things - the sides of the road, and other cars; the latter are quite content to sit still in the middle of the track, indifferent to the prospect of being rear-ended. There is a rectangular playfield. Various blocks appear slowly from the top. If one of the columns would reach the bottom, the game is over. description: From the sokoball.doc file: What is Sokoball? Sokoball is my version of the Sokoban puzzles you may have seen in the past. Sokoban is Japanese for "warehouse man". In Sokoban puzzles you must generally push a number of boxes around the screen to a designated position. The key word here is push. In Sokoban puzzles that is the only way you can move any box. You must push it to its' destination. Sokoball abides by this rule as well (in most cases). What's the object of the Sokoball game? Clear all of the boxes from the board by pushing them down the exit shafts. You are not under the gun of a clock or any number of moves. You simply must clear all boxes from the board to "beat" or solve the puzzle. I like the word beat. What are the differences between Sokoball and Sokoban? All of the Sokoban games that I have seen have offered a number of puzzles or levels that you had complete in succession. description: Videogioco "Campioni" o "A.C. Milan Football Simulator" per MS-DOS, un raro manageriale in tempo reale che permette di giocare una partita Milan-Juventus, con i veri calciatori dell'epoca, nei panni dell'allenatore del Milan. La partita viene descritta azione per azione (dura parecchio!) con testi, immagini digitalizzate e piccole animazioni. Il giocatore nel frattempo può regolare il bilanciamento attacco/difesa e l'aggressività dell'attacco, del centrocampo e della difesa, può osservare le statistiche, e di tanto in tanto gli viene richiesto di fare delle precise scelte tattiche, selezionando tra tre possibilità. After finding the source code on a backup CD and getting it to build using DOSBox, this remaster was released in 2024. It's still far from perfect by any means, but it's a much better looking, sounding and playing game overall. This version has several enhancements, optimisations and bug fixes. See the the manual for more details. This version has been optimised to run on a 486/33 with VGA Graphics Adapter, which should be: - DOSBox: “fixed 13,500” cycle CPU speed, with “vgaonly” or any of the “svga_*” machine types. - MiSTer: Default 486 Core (as of early 2024), set to 33MHz. Please check you are using these speed settings – slower or faster may lead to the game being unplayably fast or slow, or not working fully at all.

title: Iter Vehemens ad Necem
description: Iter Vehemens ad Necem (aka IVAN) means, in Latin, "Violent Road to Death". It is a Roguelike with graphics, and although rarely mentioned alongside other more well-known Roguelike examples, it seems to have a lot of polish and features. Like others in the genre, each world that you explore is unique. There are towns, dungeons, and many places to explore and, probably, die horribly. There are also a lot of keyboard commands to memorize, but you can always press ? to view a list of them. Overall it seems to have plenty of features and decent graphics (in 800x600 resolution!) as well. There is even an unofficial effort to continue developing the game (on non-DOS platforms) over at attnam.com so check that out if you're a fan of the game, there is tons of information available there.

The game is meant for two players, either against a human or against the computer, but there is also a practice mode for one player. Each cube is split into four triangles of different colours (blue, green, red, yellow) and to place one on the board the colour of each side has to match the colours of adjacent cubes. Each cube has to connect to at least one other cube. The players earn points for each cube that is placed on the board and the more sides that are connected the more points will be earned. The game is turn based and each player has a limited time (30 or 60 seconds depending on settings) and when it's out the player gets a point penalty and the opponent takes over. For each turn…

title: Baseball
description: Platform DOS Published by International PC Owners Released 1983 Genre Sports Pacing Turn-based Sport Baseball Description This computerized variant of baseball - itself based on an older BASIC adaptation from 1973 - delivers the sport to your computer screen using nothing but text. The computer and the player get to manage rival teams, and flip a coin for the home position. All input consists of numbers: when the player's team takes the field, possible throws for the pitcher are numbered 1 through 7 (fast ball, curve, slider, sinker, change-up, knuckleball, screwball). When the team is up to bat, possible actions are 1 through 4 (batter takes pitch, batter swings away, batter bunts, lead runner steals - if one is on base). The results of each move are described on screen, and after each half-inning the scoreboard is updated. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

description: Also For Apple II, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64 Developed by Tom Snyder Productions, Inc. Published by Scholastic, Inc. To win the game, the players need to work as a team to travel to Max's zone of the playfield, capture the flag, and bring it back safely back before Max is able to capture the players flag. description: Developed by Ron Dubren and Associates Platform DOS Released 1983 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Puzzle elements Description The Catacombs of Nemon is a single-player game which is entirely keyboard controlled. The game takes place on a single screen around which are scattered boulders, numbered keys, and an exit door. The player uses their torch to move around the screen and as the beam of the torch illuminates a key it's number is displayed. The player must collect the keys in sequence before they can open the door and escape to the next level. Obviously there are obstacles and in this game these take the form of rock falls which can crush the player, and a fast moving minotaur who shoots fireballs. He will either attack the player of block their passage with fire. title: Espada Sagrada, La
description: Also For Amstrad CPC, MSX, ZX Spectrum Developed by Topo Soft Published by Topo Soft Released 1990 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling, Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Fantasy Description La Espada Sagrada is an action game that consists of three phases, the third being more arcade-oriented than the first two. The protagonist Atahualpa Yupanqui aspires to obtain The Sacred Sword, and problems through the two early stages must be solved in order to find it. Then, in a third phase full of action, the hero takes advantage of that sword to be victorious. The two early stages have no side scrolling, while the third one is an arcade with horizontal scroll and non-stop action and big sprites. To access levels 2 and 3 the player needs a code, which is provided once the previous stage is finished. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Maze
description: Platform DOS Published by Ziff Davis Media Released Feb, 1983 Genre Puzzle Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description A simple maze navigation game with randomly-generated screens in 10 skill levels - 32,000 mazes are possible for each level. The player starts at the middle of the left-side wall, and must find a path towards the right side of the screen while racing against the clock; helpfully, a trail of dots is left behind the player's marker. Being not much more than a programming exercise, the game uses a rather crude algorithm to generate the mazes, so the lower difficulties will have multiple solutions, while the higher ones may have none at all. For such a contingency, the space bar will generate a new maze, though (somewhat unfairly) the clock keeps ticking while this happens. The game was published as a type-in title in PC Magazine, along with a write-up that states: "this program will probably not become a cherished family favorite". From Mobygames.com.…

In all modes gameplay is primarily concerned with bouncing a ball off a paddle on the bottom of the screen and into blocks or bricks suspended above, destroying them. In Falling Walls, as you might have been able to guess, the suspension is not complete, while in The Blast Adventure game mode, priority is on removing obstructions from around a gateway to the next level rather than on eliminating all bricks from the screen. All in all, you seem to be in a bit of a pickle. Your canteen is good for six drinks of water, unless you find a way to refill it. title: TinyTris
description: Official Site TinyTris Platform DOS Released Jul 26, 2004 Genre Action, Puzzle Gameplay Falling Block Puzzle Perspective Side view Interface Direct Control Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description TinyTris approximates the Game Boy version of Tetris as a PC game in less than 3 KB. It only implements the classic game mode, known as "A-type" in the Game Boy version: move, rotate and drop the falling 4-piece blocks, stack them in a pile at the bottom of the pit, and form complete horizontal lines to eliminate them for points. The action speeds up on each new level, but instead of leveling up every ten lines, the proverbial kick up the arse arrives at increasing intervals - you advance a level when your line count is a power of two, which means that the difficulty ramp is more gradual. title: Computer Operator
description: Platform DOS Released Oct 16, 1982 Genre Educational, Simulation Pacing Real-Time Educational Science Description This BASIC game simulates the experience of running a large, multi-user mainframe system of its day. As the operator, you first configure the system by choosing the memory size, the number of disk and tape drives, the maximum number of concurrent users, and the overall game speed. These factors determine the difficulty of your job - which is to cope with user demands and keep the system running. If too many problems pile up, the system crashes and you lose. After the system is booted, users begin to log in and do their work; you monitor the system's status in real time, and carry out your maintenance tasks using text commands. User jobs place demands on CPU time, on storage devices, and on the printer; you'll need to balance the load, repair failed equipment, bring devices offline and online as needed, and meet the users' storage requirements. title: Version (esolang) v2001.1211 for DOS
description: Version is an esoteric programming language based on the concept of ignorance-spaces . An ignorance-space is represented by a pattern (irregular expression.) All instructions in a Version program have a tag or label. Instructions with labels which match the current ignorance-space are ignored. Other instructions are executed sequentially. When the last instruction is reached, execution wraps around to the beginning of the program. The only way to halt a program is to put it in a state in which all instructions will be ignored. Other than this ignorance-space, there are no jumping or conditional execution mechanisms in Version. Esolangs.org entry: Version Technical Information This Internet Archive item runs the Version reference interpreter under Perl 5.8.8 under DOSBox. A menu is included to help demonstrate the language.

description: Word Ladders Developed by Softdisk Publishing Platform DOS Published by Softdisk Publishing Released Apr, 1991 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Word Construction Perspective Text-based / Spreadsheet Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Word Ladders is a variant on the common word puzzle in which the player must turn one word into another by changing one letter at a time, with each intervening step still being a valid English word. The game is broken into rounds which offer increasingly challenging puzzles; there is an optional Expert Mode which adds further difficulty to play. Each puzzle has a par, which is the number of steps the player is expected to need to complete a transformation. Breaking par causes a penalty to the score, while completing a puzzle quickly leads to a timer-related bonus. Players start the game with three lives, and lives are lost by running out of time or (in Expert Mode only) attempting to create an invalid word. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Combat - Conflict Simulation
description: Platform DOS Published by PC-SIG Released 1985 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Turn-based Perspective 3rd-person (Other), Top-down Setting Cold War Description A simple tactical combat simulation for two players, set upon a hex grid map. The conflict takes place in the Cold War, with six Soviet Red Army units on the offensive against a triad of cities, defended by four US Army units. Obeying certain rules, e.g. according to the type of terrain and the placement of enemy units, each side gets a movement phase and an attack phase per game turn. Combat will either eliminate one of the sides or force it to retreat; cities and woods provide a defense bonus. Both sides must meet their respective goals within 10 game turns: the Soviets win if they can occupy and hold at least two of the cities; otherwise, victory goes to the Americans. PCjr Cartridge BASIC is required to run the game. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

There are, of course, ghosts patrolling the maze and contact with them ends the game. Unlike Pac-Man there are no power pills that allow the player to overpower the ghosts, this is a puzzle game that is purely about planning a route around the maze while avoiding them. The game is entirely keyboard controlled, uses character graphics and has sound effects. title: Datnoids
description: Datnoids Platform DOS Released 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description A game of maze navigation in text mode graphics: guide your vehicle from the bottom right of the screen towards the exit at the top left, while avoiding messy encounters with the walls. The game consists of three different mazes (the first two have fixed layouts, while the third is random), and 10 skill levels are selectable - go higher and the action gets faster. Some walls can be fired at to gain passage, but others have a tendency to send your missile flying right back at you. Finish one maze, and warp to the next one - finish all three, and you'll start over at a higher speed. Considering Datnoids ' references to missiles, antimatter walls and hyperspeed jumps, any connection with the eponymous species of freshwater fish remains unclear. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: EGA Trek
description: EGA Trek is based heavily on very early computer space simulation games. (ie. the first computer game ever, Space War!, aka Computer Space). Since this is a non-licensed game, it never refers to it as "Star Trek", but you know what they were going for. It includes color graphics that although sparse do the job well. The objective is to eliminate other ships and "save the galaxy". This is a simulation/strategy game with not a lot of action, so it won't be for everyone, but it definitely is a classic PC game.

title: Bardarts
description: Platform DOS Released 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Perspective 1st-person Description Bardarts is a one or two player, shareware darts game that is based on the classic pub game of 301. In this game the player must finish on a double and the game uses the darts standard 'bust' rule, i.e. if a player's score goes below zero then all scoring darts in that turn are discarded and their score is reset. To play this game the player uses the arrow keys to position the cursor over the sector they wish to hit, the default start position is always the bulls-eye. In the lower right corner is a circular dial. The player presses the ENTER key to start the pointer on this dial moving and they must press the ENTER key twice more to stop the dial at the twelve o'clock and six o'clock positions to set the accuracy of the shot. When the game is over the player(s) are treated to a burst of music before starting again. There is no high score table, no league table, and no save game…

title: Catcher
description: Developed by Nikita Ltd. Platform DOS Published by Nikita Ltd. Released 1994 Pacing Real-Time Perspective Top-down Genre Puzzle Interface Point and Select Gameplay Arcade Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Catcher (transliterated as Кэтчер in Russian) is an arcade puzzle game. title: Contract Bridge
description: Platform DOS Released Mar 07, 1996 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Turn-based Gameplay Cards / Tiles Description Contract Bridge is a single player, shareware, implementation of the card game of the same name. The player always plays as the South hand. The game, which uses US style practices uses the Goren Point-Count method for hand evaluation and recognises these conventions; Short Club Openers, No Trump Weak Signal Bids, Preemptive Opening bids, Stayman, Take-Out Doubles, and Blackwood though any or all of these conventions can be turned off. The game opens with a suit bid on hands that have thirteen or fourteen points and a four card suit, or sixteen to eighteen points for a one no trump bid. After each hand the player can replay it, review it, or rotate the hands and replay it. The game is mouse or keyboard controlled. title: Everest - The Iceman's Apprentice
description: Developed by Cascoly Software Platform DOS Published by MVP Software Released 1996 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Managerial / Business Simulation Description Everest: The Iceman's Apprentice is a single player, shareware, mountaineering game. The game was released as shareware with just two climbs: Rainier in Washington state USA and Ama Dablam in Nepal. On registration the player received eight additional climbs including Annapurna, Kangchenjunga, and of course Everest itself. Using photographs of the actual mountains this game is essentially a management game. The player selects a group of climbers, each of which has strengths and weaknesses. They start at the base camp and assign orders to their climbers to proceed to a waypoint carrying supplies. There they may establish another camp, rest, return to base for more supplies before pushing on up the mountain. title: Fly
description: Platform DOS Released 1984 Genre Simulation Perspective 1st-person Description It spreads disease, it hangs out in your food, it has an annoying buzz. It's the common housefly, and this game wages total extermination on the nasty little bugger. One fly after the other comes dancing across your screen. Pay careful attention to its position: once it stops, you have to choose one of your three swatters to nail it with. If you succeed, you get a look at the filthy critter's splattered remains... and face off against a faster fly. If you miss, you'll have to deal with a slower one again. The more you whack, the quicker they get - if you manage to nail the fastest of them all, victory is yours! From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Gobble Man
description: Platform DOS Released 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description This text-mode BASIC game finds you in a large room littered with dots. Your character's goal is to gobble up these essential nutrients, without getting caught by the four enemies that patrol the arena. Your movements are limited to straight lines, but your foes can travel diagonally as well. The four side tunnels help you outsmart them: enter one, and you emerge at the opposite side of the playfield. More or less, Gobble Man is basically Pac-Man without the maze, or the power pills, or the extra lives: a single encounter with your ever-smiling oppressors will force you to start over from scratch. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Monsters have settled into caves and abandoned castles, villages are under attack, and one of the four islands has already been conquered. The king has hired you to help save his defenseless lands, and off you go on your quest: to find the secret of the invasion's leader, a mysterious sorcerer possessed by the a long-dead evil, and vanquish him. The four islands are connected by a teleportation bridge, and serve as the overworld, with several dungeons and caves where you'll slay monsters, gain experience levels, and find gold. description: Developed by East Wing Software Platform DOS Released 1993 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description SDI2040 is a shareware, single player, Space Invader clone . As is standard in such games, alien ships march back and forwards across the screen coming ever closer to the player's ship. The objective is to destroy all of them before they reach the bottom of the screen. There is a high score table and when the game was registered both the source code and a SoundBlaster music pack were available, each for an additional fee. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

The game is fully keyboard controlled by using dozen types of commands available. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Blockade
description: Platform DOS Released 1986 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description Blockade is a variation on the TRON -inspired Light Cycle concept, for 1 or 2 human players - computer-controlled rivals can join in for up to 6 players in total. Each player's objective is to block the others' paths with the trail left behind in their passage through the playfield - without running into their own trail, other players, or the boundary wall. A round is won when all opponents have been blockaded. Players are then scored according to their placements, and the next round begins; the first player to reach 100 points wins the game. Some parameters may be adjusted, including game speed, disappearing trails (for eliminated players), and the behavior of AI opponents. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Clock Solitaire
description: Developed by United Innovations Plus Platform DOS Released 1991 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Cards / Tiles Perspective Top-down Interface Point and Select Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description In these days where card games abound and compilations can contain hundreds of games it's easy to forget that it was not always so. Clock Solitaire is a single player, shareware game consisting of just one solitaire variant. It is played entirely with the mouse, the player clicks on the pack to deal and then moves cards around to their corresponding position in a clock face arrangement. This form of solitaire is one where there is very little strategy, success ofrfailure depends entirely upon the deal of the cards. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

This game is from the developer of Colossus Draughts which won draughts championships in the early 1990's. The game plays in CGA and EGA modes and has the following features: Games can be saved, loaded and replayed. Players can undo and redo moves - referred to in-game as 'Backward-step' and 'Forward-step'. There is a Blindfold option where the player's pieces, the AI opponent's pieces, or both are hidden any of which makes for a really odd game. The player can play against the computer or they can play both sides. There are six types of game; tournament; equal time etc, game clocks, and three types of draughts piece. One of the strengths of the early…

title: EMPIRE (IMPERO)
description: EMPIRE è un gioco del 1989 creato sulle meccaniche di Dukedom e ancora prima di "the sumer game" in cui si impersona il nobile di un paese che deve gestire tasse, popolazione, soldati e guerre per costruire il regno più prosperoso e diventare imperatore. I 6 regni possono essere comandati dal computer o da giocatori. Stando alla ricerca archeologica del sito Abandonware france (dove è anche possibile scaricare i sorgenti) questi sono i crediti del gioco: Empire è stato scritto in BASIC nel 1979 su TRS-80 da Peter Trefonas. Fu convertito per PC DOS nel 1986 da Mick Lonardo e rilasciato come freeware. La versione francese è stata scritta da Jean-Pierre Défieux il 14-08-1987 L'origine della versione italiana è ancora sconosciuta. E' stata ritrovata su un floppy dell' associazione MuPIn .
