title: Moraff's Pinball
description: Developed by Moraffware Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Pinball Description Moraff's Pinball is a single player, shareware pinball game that is entirely keyboard controlled. This is not a simulation of a real table is an early, low budget game of its type where everything is displayed on a single screen. The VGA table occupies a square in the lower left of the screen and above it there are helpful messages such as 'Light A,B,C,and D to release ball'. Over on the left of the screen is the current score game's name, high score table, a reminder of the action keys and the number of balls remaining. The player has five balls per game but if all trapped balls are released there could be as many as five balls in play at a time. The author claims it is the first game ever to support VGA in high resolution 640x480 sixteen colour mode, it also has an EGA mode which displays a slightly smaller screen and a little less information. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Mustang
description: Mustang Platform DOS Released Jul 14, 1991 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description Mustang is an arcade shooter with aircrafts. The aircraft you control is a green plane seen from above, movable over the screen using the numeric pad keys, though always oriented nose-upward on screen. Enemy aircraft come single or in formations of different sizes and from all directions, sometimes turning, sometimes just flying straight past, shooting bullets and rockets at your plane. There are also power-up objects that fall from the top of the screen, like health-packs to replenish your life-meter, missiles and 3-way guns that you can pick up by passing over them, and these will change your fire-mode for a limited time. When you eventually get shot down, you may end up on a high-score list. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Super Trix
description: Platform DOS Published by Yedioth Ahronoth Released 1993 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Super Trix is a promotional game of the Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth , in collaboration with Coca-Cola. The player controls Super Trix on his quest to recover the six missing sections of the newspaper and has to go through each of the levels while dealing with hostile bees, thunderbolts, and other dangers. Super Trix's health is represented by Coca-Cola cans, which can be collected throughout the levels for recovery. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Crypto Cube
description: Platforms Apple II, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64, PC Booter Developed by DesignWare, Inc. Published by DesignWare, Inc. Released 1983 Genre Educational, Puzzle Gameplay Word Construction Educational Reading / Writing Description 20 themed words are arranged in criss-cross formation over the faces of a three-dimensional cube. You have to guess and uncover them. A mascot- The Wuzzle- apprises you of your progress. When uncovering the words, you will get: a blank square- no points and the turn is over; a vowel- 5 points and another turn; a consonant- you get a question mark and must guess the letter- a correct guess nets 10 points and another turn, an incorrect guess -5 points and the turn is over. There are also bonus squares that let you pick an extra square on the current cube-side, as well as one on another side. New word lists can be added by the user- ostensibly to allow children to practice their spelling homework. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Tiào Ch'i translates to "jump chess", and computer AI players are given the names of deities from the ancient Chinese pantheon. Each player controls a contingent of numbered tiles, but in the graphical version these can be replaced with pictorial tokens, representing the 12 animal signs of the Chinese zodiac. 2 to 6 players may participate, with each player attempting to relocate all his tokens to the opposite side of the star-shaped game board. title: Tommy's Crosswords
description: Developed by Tommy's Toys Platform DOS Released 1986 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Word Construction Perspective Text-based / Spreadsheet Interface Text Parser Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Tommy's Crosswords is a single-player crossword game. This game comes with thirty-nine pre-made crosswords and an editor so that players can create and share their own puzzles. In Solution mode it has two cheat modes, one gives the player the current letter, as indicated by the cursor, and the other gives the entire word. In Creation mode there's an optional encryption feature to prevent others cheating. There are also two command line switches one to force a colour display and another to force a monochrome display. title: Chain Reaction
description: Platform DOS Released Aug 14, 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Description Chain Reaction is a shareware strategy game for one or two people. The game is played on an 8x8 grid into which players take turns to place their counters. Each square can hold as many counters as it has neighbours horizontally and vertically. Once a cell has been claimed by a player it belongs to them unless a neighbouring cell is over filled. A cell that is overfilled explodes leaving just one counter behind, the remaining counters move into all the neighbouring cells swapping which change to the colour of the new token. If they in turn become over filled they explode and so on and so on until a state of stability is reached The object of the game is to eliminate the opposition by converting all counters to the player's colour. The game is played with the mouse and has optional, basic, sound effects From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

description: Developed by New Line Software Platform DOS Published by New Line Software Released 1990 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Plexu: The Time Travellers is a DOS conversion of the Amiga title of the same name . The gameplay remains unchanged with only one significant change. Instead of a side-scrolling perspective the player sees the action divided into numerous single board locations with a level boss at the end. Plexu may walk, jump, use a single, double and supershot gun plus - killing all enemies on board - Smartbomb and temporary invulnerability. Between each level the player may purchase various extras in the Intergalactic Shop, including extra life or time, needed to complete subsequent stage. Fighting with the final stage boss requires targeting an opponent's head and avoiding numerous incoming missiles. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: ASCII Invaders
description: ASCII Invaders is, as you might expect, an interpretation of the classic Space Invaders game using nothing but ASCII characters in text-mode. The gameplay is the same as the classic arcade game: Shoot the invaders and dodge their shots as they methodically move left and right as a group, slowly inching their way towards the bottom of the screen. (At least until the last few, when they start to speed up.) There is some animation here as well as some satisfying PC speaker sound effects. It also adds the feature of various types of "bombs" that can be used to clear away invaders, as well as removing the shields that are typically part of this sort of game. (The author notes that this game was programmed in using the Pascal programming language.)

title: Fencing
description: Developed by OR Concepts Applied Platform DOS Released Jun, 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Description Fencing is a shareware strategy game for one or two players. The game is played on a game area consisting of one hundred and one parallel horizontal lines, numbered from AA to EA, and seventy one vertical lines, numbered 01 - 71. Players take turns to specify sets of co-ordinates, the objective of the game being to create triangles, the winner of the game being the player who has enclosed the greatest area at the end of the game. The computer opponent has five difficulty settings, there is a save/load function and optional sound effects. The game has a countdown timer which the player(s) can adjust for shorter or longer games. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

To make things more challenging, the player has a limited number of moves in each direction (which varies from level to level and by difficulty setting). title: Clonk 2 - Debakel
description: Developed by RedWolf Design Platform DOS Published by RedWolf Design Released Oct, 1994 Genre Action, Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Perspective Side view, Top-down Description The sequel to Clonk adds a new game element to the concept. The classic action-oriented melee rounds are now part of a larger strategy part. Two to four players each get their own troops of Clonks, with which they set out to conquer towns and castles in a predefined or randomly generated hexagon map. Whenever two troops of hostile players meet on a specific field of the game's map, the game switches to a combat round, in which both players take direct control over their Clonks to eliminate the opposite crew. Crew strength, landscape and weather depend on the actual situation in the strategy part. Players also have to worry about taxes, diplomatics and the happiness of the population in their controlled territories. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Endless Night, The
description: Developed by MythicArt Software Platform DOS Published by MythicArt Software Released 1993 Genre Adventure Gameplay Puzzle elements Perspective 3rd-person (Other), Top-down Setting Fantasy Description The Endless Night is a top-down adventure game that starts without a back story as the main character wakes up with amnesia in a pitch black world. His only goals are to find out who he is and unravel the mystery behind the endless night. The only controls are the arrow keys to walk around. For most of the game, the screen is completely black with only the player illuminated for movement as he stumbles through the maze like map, occasionally bumping into items or someone to talk to. Eventually, should the player happen upon it, there is town where he can get a lantern that allows the player to fully see the map. From this point on, the game becomes fairly straightforward, searching the map for items and completing fetch quests for the villagers to advance the plot. From Mobygames.com.…

title: MS-DOS: Alf's Party Kit
description: Alf's Party Kit is a fun collection of mini applications and games that are designed, as the name suggests, to help kids print invitations and banners for parties and have fun playing mini party games with their friends. With the help of Alf, the lovable alien from a hit TV series, kids can design decorations using a range of fonts, color palettes, and Alf cartoons, as well as print invitations for their friends, guest list, party checklist, and various stationery items. The games included in the program are designed to be printed out on paper for kids to play, and are all fun - although they are more arcade-style than educational. Kids can print out a color-the-tail game and a nice little maze game, among other things. All in all, a comprehensive little party kit that predates Kid Pix and similar programs by a few years. Recommended if you have Alf fans in your house, although the 4-color CGA palette may turn them off (not to mention incompatibility with modern printers).

title: PolyMaze
description: Developed by RollinSoft Platform DOS Published by RollinSoft Released Apr 05, 1983 Genre Puzzle Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description For maze maniacs who are bored of rectangular layouts and right angles, PolyMaze generates mazes in a multitude of different shapes, from a triangle to a 61-vertex polygon. Mazes are solved by traversing them along a grid, from a point on the perimeter towards the center, and each maze can contain 2 to 18 levels along the way; a later version of the game allows players to save their progress and retrieve it later, in case they get lost. Those who don't feel like doing their own path-finding may hand the task over to the computer, or just watch random mazes being generated. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Tommy's Fan Tan
description: Developed by Tommy's Toys Platform DOS Released 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Cards / Tiles Description Tommy's Fan Tan is a shareware card game for three to eight players, if less than three players participate the computer plays the remaining positions so that at least three players are in the game. This version of the game contains the original game plus the Sevens/Parliament, Five or Nine, Pay or Play variants. The game is played with a standard deck but in Fan Tan the Ace counts as the lowest card in the deck. It is played for chips and continues until only one player has some chips left, naturally that player is the winner. The whole pack is dealt out, so some players have one more card than others and, briefly, the games are played as follows: Sevens: The 7 card is the foundation card for any suit. title: Tonko
description: Developed by TWIM Platform DOS Published by Nesco Released Jan, 1994 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform Description Tonko is a Korean-made platform game that consists of very small (almost single-screen) stages. Each stage is a platform structure populated by monsters. The player controls a cute yellow goblin who must defeat these monsters, traveling through stages with real-world geographical backgrounds. Among the enemies are Nazi ghosts, vampires, beer mugs, American football helmets, crazy fish, and other unorthodox creatures. Tonko can jump and whack enemies on the head with his hammer, which can be upgraded with various power-ups (such as electricity charge) scattered around the stages. If an enemy touches Tonko, he loses a life; the game is over when Tonko has no lives left. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Worm Burner
description: Platform DOS Published by COMPUTE! Publications, Inc. Released Oct, 1987 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description An adaptation of Gridrunner , where the player is assigned to defend Earth from a herd of ravenous space worms, who have apparently developed a particular appetite for the planets of the Solar System. Action takes place along a grid; the player's ship is free to move about its bottom rows, though it can only fire upwards. Each attack wave brings more of the marauding creatures into the fray. The worms descend from the top in Centipede -like fashion, weaving and winding across the playfield. Knocking out a worm segment will only split the creature in two; the blasted segment will keep blocking traffic as it mutates. Eventually it will fall off the grid, destroying everything in its path. The defense grid is equipped with two automatic laser guns, which prowl the edges and attempt to zap the…

description: Developed by SiEn Art Platform DOS Published by C&M; Entertainment Co. Released 1995 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Side view Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Into the Sun: Projected Distruction ( sic ) is a Korean-made horizontally-scrolling shooter similar to IAS . The player controls a fighter craft that flies above planet surfaces and traverses hostile bases in order to avert a threat imposed by an alien force on humanity. The preceding game's secondary weapon that specifically targeted enemy missiles has been replaced by a more conventional powerful all-screen attack. Missiles, smart bombs, and satellite guns are not available as power-ups any more, and must be purchased in a store between stages. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Kengi
description: Also For Amiga Developed by Software 2000 Published by Software 2000 Released 1991 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Visual Isometric Description Kengi is a Othello variant played with little aliens instead of stones. As with the original board game, the players place the aliens in turns on a 8x8 board with the goal to have the most own aliens on the field when the match ends. An alien has to be placed besides another alien already on the field and all of the hostile aliens between the placed and next own alien are turned into own aliens, The main variation are five instead of one board. They can be reached through a panel on the right which also shows a small preview of the already placed aliens. The placement rules between the boards remain identical in vertical order. There is only one board on screen at a time. There are three difficulty levels and an optional time limit for each turn. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Legacy of the Necromancer - Part I - The Adventurers' Museum
description: Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Adventure Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure Setting Fantasy Description In Legacy of the Necromancer: Part I - The Adventurers' Museum , the player visits a museum which holds 20 of the most famous treasures of all time. Well, at least it did until the last renovation during which the protective spells had to be disengaged. A wizard took this opportunity and summoned an imp which promptly stole all treasure! The player's goal is to explore the nearby cave and bring it back. In order to win the game, the player needs to solve puzzles by collecting items (the inventory can hold six) and entering commands into the parser. It supports most commands and abbreviations found in Zork . Like in those classic adventure games, the player can die and render the game unwinnable with certain moves. Resource management (determined by the number of moves) includes thirst, hunger, air (when underwater) and lamp power. This game is first part of the Legacy…

title: IAS
description: Developed by Sigmatec Platform DOS Published by Sigmatec Released 1994 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Side view Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description IAS is a sci-fi horizontally scrolling shoot-em-up. The player controls a fighter craft, defending a human space colony against the onslaught of enemy ships and mechas. The gameplay is similar to most other games of the genre and involves shooting or avoiding the incessantly advancing enemy craft while collecting power-ups on the way. The latter are distinguished by their color and change the player character's weapons, including laser fire, missiles, a slow yet powerful charged energy shot, etc. The secondary weapon has to be activated with a separate button and functions somewhat differently than in other comparable games, specifically targeting enemy missiles. The player character's health is measured by an energy bar; once it is depleted, the game is over. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Indecent
description: Developed by LAAL Software Engineers Platform DOS Published by LAAL Software Engineers Released Mar 17, 1995 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Indecent packs an arcade flying game with 256 different levels, parallax scrolling, and procedurally generated terrain, into the rather tight space of 256 bytes of machine code. The idea is to get your starship safely across an increasingly dangerous environment, plagued by floating junk (yellow dots) and by cave walls that gradually start closing in the further you travel. The white, pixelly ship can only be moved up or down to avoid these obstacles - any collision spells instantaneous doom; a progress bar at the bottom tells you how much of the level you've traveled. Various levels may be loaded by specifying different ASCII characters as a command-line parameter. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Snakes
description: Official Site Snakes Platform DOS Published by RufusPro Software Released 1988 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Snakes is a Tandy 1000 BASIC game firmly in the 'arena collector' tradition: you control a continuously-moving critter roaming a fenced-off area, whose task is to pick up as many collectibles as possible without dying in the process. To survive, it is enough to avoid the edges of the playfield and the spiky, sharp-looking protrusions strewn throughout it. The title may lead one to expect a Snake-type game where the creature's body grows as it feeds; this is not so -- your on-screen incarnation always occupies a single grid position. Only one level is included, and you're granted five lives to make the most of it. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Space Snake
description: Developed by Ediciones Manali, S.A. Platform DOS Published by Ediciones Manali, S.A. Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Top-down Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description A plague of Space snakes wants to reconquer the Mars Planet. In the role of a brave spaceship pilot, part of the defence line of the planet, the player must resist the attack of ten hordes of this violent monsters. Each horde is stronger than the previous one. The player has only 5 spaceships to vanquish the attack of the space snakes. The gameplay is very simple. Our ship only can move in the horizontal axis (like "Galaxian"), and player must destroy all the Space Snakes, while avoiding the enemy assaults. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

(As the game was originally written as an MS-DOS batch file, the text parser is necessarily quite limited, as is the overall scope of the game.) From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Released Jun, 1985 Genre Strategy/Tactics Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description To humans of the far future, the forgotten planet Earth is nothing but an old tale. That is, until a lucky explorer stumbles into the lost blue sphere... but will signs of ancient habitation be found? It's time to break out your three trusty Archeodroids - excavation robots programmed to retrieve archeological evidence. description: Developed by SoftLab Laboratories Platform DOS Published by SoftLab Laboratories Released 1991 Genre Action, Adventure, Role-Playing (RPG) Gameplay Shooter Perspective 1st-person Narrative Spy / Espionage Description The Nine Lives of Secret Agent Katt is a role playing game with adventure and action elements mixed in. Your team consists of 4 spies, each with their own talents, tools and weapons: Katt (the leader), Tia, Roco and Mad Dog. Your primary mission: to recover stolen documents from a fortified secret laboratory and make it out alive. Adventure type puzzles involve choosing the proper team member, actions and inventory objects to use. Some objects can be combined to create an entirely new item. title: Racecar
description: Platform DOS Published by International PC Owners Released 1983 Genre Racing / Driving Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description If you've ever felt like challenging your IBM to a race, look no further than Race Car to get your speed thrills in 40-column ASCII graphics. The action takes place on a figure-8 race track, where one player competes for a single lap against the computer, represented by a smiling face (the computer holds the title of champion, which explains the mirth). Your car steers and turns automatically -- the only controls are speeding up and braking. Turning corners at unsafe speeds may result in a crash, which can set you back valuable time. The first to cross the finish line wins the race; 3 difficulty levels are available, plus a demonstration mode for those who prefer the role of spectators. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Rocks
description: Official Site Rocks Developed by ASM Software Platform DOS Published by ASM Software Released 1997 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective Top-down Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Rocks is an Asteroids clone. Much like in the zap-'em-up hit from the arcades, you find yourself inexplicably trapped in a rectangular region of space that wraps around on itself on all four sides, populated by successive waves of asteroids being hurled in random directions. Your turn and thrust controls allow your ship to cruise around the playfield, equipped with a frontal mounted blaster to dispatch the wandering lumps of space rock. You can also brake to restrain your inertial motion. Blasting apart a large rock causes it to split in two, and the same goes for the resulting fragments, until the smallest chunks are eliminated. Each consecutive wave brings more asteroids into play, and occasionally a suspiciously-square alien craft will drop in to menace you as well. From Mobygames.com.…

title: Purple Martians
description: Purple Martians is a platforming game, described by its author as being "like Bubble Bobble or Mario". I disagree with that assessment, but it's still a decently fun game. The goal is to get to the exit, blasting baddies on the way. You'll need to destroy all enemies on the level before making it to the exit. They will drop powerups to help you. Although the game's graphics are not the highest quality, they do have a sort of charm about them. And the game itself plays well and offers 35 levels, and even includes a level editor (separate from the main game program) so you can make your own levels.

title: Generic Adventure 551
description: Also For Amiga Released Sep, 1990 Genre Adventure Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure, Puzzle elements Setting Fantasy Description Generic Adventure 551 is a version of the classic interactive fiction game Adventure (also known as Colossal Cave Adventure ). It is based on Dave Long 's 350 point Fortran version (1978) which was later (around 1984) expanded to 551 points by different authors The code was later touched by Doug McDonald so it could be compiled with Fortran translation tools and released to the Usenet in August 1990. His code was then ported to other platforms. The basic content does not differ from the original: the player searches a mysterious cave for treasure. This requires exploring the environment and solving puzzles by typing in commands into a parser. The DOS port adds the ability to save the game to different files and the Amiga ports has a different front-end. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: aMpSuX
description: aMpSuX, also known as AMP Killers, was one of the first video games I ever made. I was probably all of 14 years old, possibly younger, when I made it. It was actually a present for my mom who was extremely frustrated with a garbage Point of Sales program she had to use as part of her job. Long short short, hop in a chopper, fly to the headquarters of said POS POS vendor, set a bomb, and blow it up. This was made in Virtual Reality Studio 1.0 (the North American commercially available version of the Freescape game engine) and yes, it was a legal copy I got bundled with the book Garage Virtual Reality by Linda Jacobson. I recommend running this in DosBox or PCEm or on a real 486 in MS-DOS 6.22 or Windows 95's DOS mode. Works fantastic on the ao486 core in MiSTer FPGA as well. The AmPsUXDOSBOX.zip includes a pre-configured DosBox. Just run ampsux.exe. If you want to go old school, download aMpSuX.zip instead and extract that to your MS-DOS or Windows 95 or whatever computer. The…

title: Bird Brain
description: Also For Apple II, Commodore 64, TI-99/4A Developed by Emerald Valley Publishing Co. Published by Emerald Valley Publishing Co. Released Dec, 1984 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Take control of a hungry tropical bird, prowling for a succulent meal while on a break from brooding on her eggs. Catching that fat fish swimming leisurely in the river below isn't a trivial task: the bird can only be directed by flapping its wings, in a manner similar to Joust , with additional momentum control to the right or left. Any imprecise movement, and the famished avian may find an untimely demise beneath the waters, or be swept aside by an onrushing wave. Once a fish is picked up, it must be brought back to the nest within the time limit, or the bird will die. The quicker your performance, the higher your score, which multiplies with the difficulty level; higher levels speed up the action and make the bird harder to control. From…

title: BooTris
description: Platform PC Booter Released Feb 14, 1993 Genre Action, Puzzle Gameplay Falling Block Puzzle Perspective Side view Interface Direct Control Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description This super-small version of Tetris is written to fit into the 512-byte boot sector of a floppy disk. Assembly source code is included with the game, along with a program to install it onto any diskette. The basic elements of Tetris are all here: the falling blocks can be rotated, moved and dropped to complete solid horizontal lines; the filled-up lines are cleared away to make room for more, and to prevent the pile from growing to the top of the playfield. However, the game doesn't keep score, doesn't show you the next piece, and doesn't speed up as you progress - these non-essentials have been dispensed with, making the game small enough to self-boot in half a kilobyte (without taking up any of the disk's visible space at all). From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Multiplex
description: Developed by Aestan Games Platform DOS Published by Aestan Games Released Sep 01, 2007 Genre Action, Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Multiplex is something of a cross between Beast 's monster-squashing action and Pyro II 's explosion-happy pyromania; much like those two games, it's rendered in colorful ASCII graphics. You, the player, find yourself in a series of mazes populated by roving monsters - all of whom must be killed. One way to do this is to crush them with the assortment of pushable walls scattered throughout each level. The second (and more entertaining) method is to step in close to them, which causes them to self-destruct in a dazzling explosion. This is best done carefully, because the explosions are deadly; if other monsters (or eggs) are caught in the blast they'll explode as well, setting off chain reactions. Later levels feature large, scrolling playfields, packed with faster enemies that detonate in…

description: Platform DOS Released 1993 Genre Puzzle Pacing Real-Time Description Amazing is a single player, shareware, maze game. title: Crosscheck
description: Platforms Apple II, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64, DOS Developed by IntelliCreations, Inc., Xel-Ha Associates Published by Datasoft, Inc. Released Aug, 1986 Pacing Turn-based Perspective Text-based / Spreadsheet Genre Puzzle Interface Text Parser Gameplay Word Construction Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Crosscheck is a trivia and word-based strategy game for 1 - 4 players for multiple platforms. A combination of a crossword puzzle, and Scrabble, the players take turns rolling a dice numbered 1 - 9. Depending on the roll, they will be asked a trivia question, or allowed to directly post a tile on the table. The player's answer will always be as long as the number rolled. title: Hide and Sink
description: Developed by Mirror Images Software, Inc. Platform DOS Published by Mirror Images Software, Inc. Released 1983 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Turn-based Perspective 3rd-person (Other), Top-down Gameplay Board Game Vehicular Naval / Watercraft Description The pen-and-paper game Battleship gets another digital translation, which pits man against machine for a round of grid-based marine warfare. Both sides get five ships each - of varying sizes - and hide them within their respective game boards, invisible to the opponent. Each side then proceeds to fire in turn, by selecting a target grid position. When all the squares occupied by a ship are hit, it is sunk; the first player to destroy the entire enemy fleet will rule the waves. title: Triskelion
description: Platform DOS Released 1987 Genre Puzzle Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Triskelion is a single player freeware puzzle game. Triskelion is a genetic word for any device or motif which has three symbols that share a common centre. This can be curved arms, or legs in the case of the symbol common to the Isle of Man (UK). In this case it is three overlapping circles. Each circle is comprised of squares, called marbles in the documentation. Each marble has its own colour (blue, green and red). A fourth colour (yellow) is used for the centre of the design where all three circles overlap. The object of the puzzle is to find a way to rotate all the yellow segments out of the central area and replace them with another single colour. The game is entirely controlled by the keyboard and has no sound and no save/load feature. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Battle Charge
description: Developed by Cold Water Software Platform DOS Released 1993 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Real-Time, Turn-based Description Battle Charge is a two player, shareware, strategy game which is so named because two players fight it out using charged tokens. The game area is a 16x10 grid that is completely filled with two sets of counters, one red and the other blue; these fill opposite halves of the screen so that there are 8x10 red counters in one half and 8x10 blue counters in the other. In opposite corners sit pale red and pale blue counters, these are the king pieces of each player. The player fires a token by clicking on it and drawing the mouse back to set a direction and velocity. Most collisions cause the tokens to change place but under certain conditions the player can combine them thus converting their basic tokens into charged pieces. title: Intergalactic Bar Mans Pub Crawl
description: Platform DOS Released 1991 Genre Adventure Gameplay Puzzle elements Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Intergalactic Bar Mans Pub Crawl is a single player, shareware, adventure game. The player takes the role of a bar man on an intergalactic cruiser. One morning they awake to find the ship deserted and the object of the game is to try to escape from the ship alive. To do this they explore the ship using the traditional N, S, W, and E keys for North South etc as well as talking to the ship's computer. The game area consists of two sections. The lower part describes the current location and is where the player enters their commands. The upper part shows the inventory, a map of the space cruiser which is drawn automatically as the player progresses through the game, and a small diagram representing the current room. title: MaxMan
description: Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Description MaxMan is a single player, shareware, Pac-Man clone. As with other Pac-Man games the player runs around a maze, eating power ups, and generally avoiding the nasty green gremlins unless they have eaten a big power up in which case they go monster hunting. This game adds a minor twist in that when the player loses a life their ghost lives on as a 'grim reaper' and becomes one of the nasties that has to be killed. The higher the player's score when all the gremlins and ghosts have been killed the more baddies they will face in the next round. The game is keyboard controlled and has basic sound effects such as bleeps, whistles and so-on. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Trivia 2000
description: Developed by TAK Theory Platform DOS Released 1986 Genre Educational Description Trivia 2000 is a shareware game based on Trivial Pursuit. When a round begins the game simulates the roll of the dice after which it checks forwards and backwards from the players position and determines which way they should move. Having 'moved' the player the game then announces the category and asks the question. Questions are answered in the normal way by typing in the answer using the standard keys. Two things make this game different to other implementations of Trivial Pursuit, the first being that there is no representation of the game board and the other is that the game's menu options are selected via the function keys. The game has a save/load function which in game parlance is referred to as freeze/unfreeze. A second edition of this game was produced, it had questions on People & Music but no changes in gameplay. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Y
description: Platform DOS Released 1994 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Arcade Description Y is a game based on the divide and conquer principle. Each level starts as a blue area surrounded with a thin green border. The player is represented by a small white ball, and when it moves into the blue area, it trails a purple "tail." Once the ball moves back into the green, any empty blue area cut off by the tail becomes green as well. If the area is not empty, only the tail itself turns green. There are red balls moving in the blue area, and black balls moving around the green area. The player starts with three lives, and has 3 minutes to turn 75% of the blue area to green. The player loses a life when the white ball touches a green or red ball, when a red ball touches the purple tail, or when the clock runs out. The player gains a life by finishing a level without losing any lives, or by getting an "extra life" power up. Power ups appear randomly in the blue area for a short amount of time, and…

Unfortunately, the tomb's current residents aren't on board with Buster's scientific curiosity. He finds himself chased around by the jumping skull of Amin Ramen himself, a cobra (named Sam), and a scorpion (whom we do not know on a first-name basis). To complete a level, Buster has to color all the pyramid blocks *and* collect the urn that appears at the top now and then. title: Dustman
description: Platform DOS Released 1992 Genre Puzzle Pacing Real-Time Perspective Top-down Interface Direct Control Visual 2D scrolling Description Dustman is a single player, shareware, puzzle game. The player is presented with a game area on which there are houses, paths and areas of grass. The player must collect from all of the houses around the town. Points are scored for bins and bin-bags collected, points are lost for dropped or split bags which can happen if too many bags are being carried. There are also dogs around the town which may, or may not, attack. description: Official Site Quasar Platform DOS Published by RufusPro Software Released 1990 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective 1st-person Vehicular Space Flight Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Perhaps notable for a valiant effort at real-time, wireframe 3-D graphics in (Tandy 1000) BASIC, Quasar is a first-person space shooter taking place across multiple quadrants of an unnamed galactic sector. Your fighter is equipped with limited energy stores, and a double laser (which depletes said energy). You start off in a planetary sector populated by waves of hostiles, which come in two chief variants: yellow and red; both take pleasure in ramming you, with bad results for your continuing existence. Destroying the red craft increases your energy however, while picking off the yellows engages your warp drive. title: Tommy's Cryptoquips
description: Developed by Tommy's Toys Platform DOS Released 1992 Genre Puzzle Pacing Turn-based Perspective Text-based / Spreadsheet Gameplay Word Construction Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Tommy's Cryptoquips is a shareware code breaking game that is based on the 'Cryptograms' that are popular in some newspapers and puzzle books. The game displays a quotation that has been encrypted by a form of letter substitution code, and the player's task is to decode it. It can be played as a single player game or as a team game for two to six players. Every quotation comes with at least one letter decoded. The game is entirely keyboard controlled. It has a demo mode which displays coded quotations but does not attempt to solve them, basic sound effects and command line switches to start the game with sound turned off and to force either a colour or monochrome display. title: British Square
description: Platform DOS Released 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Turn-based Description British Square is a single player, strategy game that is played against the computer on a 5x5 grid. Players take turns placing pieces on to the grid until neither has a valid move remaining. There are only two rules: The first move of the game may not be to the centre square. A player cannot move to a square that faces another player's piece The winner is the player who placed the most pieces, they score the difference between the number of pieces they placed and the number placed by their opponent. The winner of a match is the first to score seven points The game has music and a command-line parameter to play in 'easy' mode. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Catch88
description: Platform DOS Released Dec, 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Description This catch-the-falling-objects game uses almost the entire keyboard for its controls. An assortment of ASCII characters is raining down from the sky, and your job is to catch as many as you can: each column of the screen is marked by a letter or a number, and you can instantly move your basket to any position on the floor by pressing the corresponding key. The various symbols have different point values, but you're only allowed 21 misses, so they're all equally important to catch. The game can be played in 40 or 80-column modes, and offers four difficulty levels. When the game is over, you're awarded with a short interlude from the speaker, depending on your score - and if you were good enough, the computer will adjust for your skill by making each level twice as difficult! From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: The Book of Mormon Game (1988)
description: This is an educational game designed to help players learn about the the Book of Mormon, the game resembles a multi-player board game which uses characters, quotes, and stories from the book. Three skill levels are included to allow the game to accommodate players whether or not they are familiar with the Book of Mormon. Players start by choosing one of the available characters from the Book of Mormon (a short biography of each character is available as well). Once all players have a character, the gameboard is shown which features a long, winding path representing the journey of Lehi's family to reach the promised land. On each turn players start by rolling a dice (in a typical computer dice fashion, the screen shows two dice with rapidly changing dots; pressing a key stops it). The players character will the move forward by the number of spaces shown on the dice. Based on the space, the computer will show an event from the Book of Mormon along with the approximate date it occurred…

title: Bullseye
description: Platforms DOS, Mainframe Developed by Digital Equipment Corporation Published by Digital Equipment Corporation Released 1973 Genre Simulation, Sports Pacing Turn-based Gameplay Board Game Description Bullseye is a simple text-based simulation of the perennial pub game of Darts, for up to 20(!) players. The target board is divided into zones of 10, 20, 30 and 40 points, and each player in turn selects a move: fast overarm, controlled overarm, or underarm - the type of throw dictates the probable outcome. Once all throws have been scored, a new round begins, until one or more players win by reaching 200 points. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Dots
description: Developed by TumbleWeed Software Platform DOS Released 1992 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Description Dots is a shareware strategy game similar to Reversi . Players start with counters on the corners of a 7x7 grid. The players have counters of different colours. Each player can move any piece of their colour to any other unoccupied cell in one of two ways. Moving a piece to any adjacent square causes the piece will be duplicated, resulting in the player owning two pieces, whereas moving two squares away just causes the piece to be moved. Players can capture another player's piece by moving one of their pieces to one of the eight squares surrounding the other player's piece. The player with the most pieces on the board at the end of the game is the winner. The game is mouse controlled. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Killer Bees
description: Platform DOS Released 1992 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Shooter Perspective 1st-person Description In this simple mouse-driven shooter, you protect a man who enjoys hanging out under hives full of angry bees. Not the brightest thing to do, perhaps, since he also seems to be rather allergic - a single sting will make him drop dead on the spot. Be that as it may, the bees attack in groups of four, and your job is to pick them off in the air using your crosshair. Try to exterminate as many as you can before one of them reaches the man and puts an end to his poorly-chosen hobby. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Power Putt
description: Developed by Clubware Platform DOS Released 1992 Genre Sports Pacing Turn-based Perspective Top-down Sport Golf Description Power Putt is a shareware, computerised version of crazy golf. The game is controlled by a combination of keyboard controls and the mouse. Taking a shot is broken down into the following tasks. The position on the tee is selected via the number keys the arrow keys are then used to set the direction of the shot finally there are two power bars which control the power and accuracy of the shot, these are set by either the ENTER key or a mouse button. Shots taken on the green are identical but, obviously, omit the tee selection stage. The game keeps track of the player. The game was released as single player, shareware game with just five holes while the full game which has eighteen holes and caters for more players was available upon registration. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Tommy's Chess Set
description: Developed by Tommy's Toys Platform DOS Released 1986 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Description Tommy's Chess Set is a shareware, chess game which uses character graphics. It is fairly natural when thinking about chess games to think of programs like IBM's Deep Blue and others of its kind, games that play chess well enough to give anyone from an amateur to a grand master a good game. Tommy's Chess Set is not that kind of a game as it does not actually play chess itself. What it does is give the player a computerised chess set with which they can play against another player on the same, or another machine. Alternatively a player can set up a board representing a chess puzzle or a famous game and play it to its conclusion. The game uses standard chess notation and has save and restore functions as well as back-step and undo back-step functions. Players can also add their own notes to each move and review these when replaying a game. The game is entirely keyboard controlled.…

title: Cavalcade O' Card Games 2.5r
description: Cavalcade O' Card Games 2.5r, by Derek Duban. This is the registered version, but the author made the registered version freely available: "Would you be willing to allow legal redistribution of the registered version of Cavalcade O' Card Games? That makes it much easier to back it up long-term. This doesn't need to be anything formal, just saying that the registered version can be distributed freely is good enough." "Hi. Yes, you may distribute them freely provided that they are not sold. So go ahead, distribute freely - no problem. I would also like a link on the page if possible. I think that I've hinted to you that I'm building a new game development studio for casual games. Links to it would be really helpful later." The studio in question is https://playscl.com/ This was taken from the floppy image on archive.org, and repackaged to be playable online. The file dates are wrong, but the floppy disk file dates were also wrong.

title: Frantis - Mission II
description: Developed by Omega Integral Systems Platform DOS Released 1993 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade, Platform, Shooter Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Frantis: Mission II is a side-scrolling platform game which continues the story of MegaDestroyer Frantis . As the main character's craft is shot down over planet Rakbet IV he bails out in an escape pod and lands right in an underground enemy base. He must now continue his mission on foot, proceeding deeper into the complex in order to destroy it from the inside. Typical for the genre, the gameplay of Frantis: Mission II consists of navigating two-dimensional levels, collecting powerups, keycards and fighting various enemies. It is possible to buy powerups in terminals that can be sometimes find in the levels. The game only has a single-player mode. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Osbit
description: Developed by STD Research Platform DOS Published by Future Publishing Limited Released Nov, 1988 Genre Action Gameplay Platform Description Osbit is a single-player, freeware, keyboard controlled, runny jumpy platform game. Osbit is an operating system bit who lives inside a computer. After a power surge struck the computer Osbit found himself a long way from home and must now fight his way, the power surge released nasty bugs, through the three levels of corrupted areas of DOS back to the A-prompt and home. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: PChallenge
description: Platform DOS Published by Software Communications, Inc. Released Jun, 1982 Genre Action Gameplay Paddle / Pong Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Written as a 16-line BASIC program published in PC Magazine, PChallenge may be described as Pong without the second player, or Breakout without the bricks, or both. The player controls a paddle, which can be moved along the bottom of the screen to deflect a moving ball and bounce it off the walls; lose all ten balls, and it's game over. The paddle comes in 3 selectable sizes, and the ball speed is controlled by an adjustable drag factor - the longer the game, the faster the action gets. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Fairy Godmom
description: This is definitely a unique puzzle game. In it you play a fairy godmother ("Woah, couldn't have figured that out on my own", you say) who must collect magic coins on each board while avoiding killer crabs. (!?!) Anywho, the idea is to use your magic wand to "copy" objects and create them elsewhere to allow you to progress. (It makes sense when you actually play the game. Well, not the evil crabs stuff, but the magic wand stuff.) Neat game. (It used to be listed here as "Fairy Godmother" but that full title isn't used in the game itself.)

title: Robots the Game
description: Robots the Game (or simply "BOT" on the title screen) is a simple chase game done in text mode (except the title screen) which plays similarly to Autobots and others games like it. The object is to make the robots crash into each other; they will relentlessly chase you, and you'll need to move carefully (and use your limited "jumps" which move you to a random location) to destroy them all and move on to the next level.

title: Losing Your Grip
description: Also For Macintosh, OS/2, Windows Released Feb 15, 1998 Genre Adventure Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure Description In Losing Your Grip , the protagonist, Terry, is in rehab for nicotine addiction. When the game begins, Terry is standing in a muddy glade as the rain pours down. Soon, a human head, buried up in the mud, explains, mysteriously, that Terry has "pieces to recover", and he is left to his own devices. Losing Your Grip is an interactive fiction game. Commands, like go north , are entered into a text parser, and the game responds with text as well. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Weekend Survival
description: Platform DOS Released Jun 13, 1995 Genre Adventure, Educational Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure Perspective Text-based / Spreadsheet Interface Text Parser Setting Contemporary Description Weekend Survival is a text adventure set in Newark, Delaware where the player takes on the role of a student of the English Language Institute, with many things to do over the course of one weekend, including classwork that must be completed for Monday morning. Your first choice after getting your assignment at the end of class on Friday is whether you immediately leave to be with your friends, or stick around in the classroom and get more information from your teacher about the assignment. Instead of typing in full commands, you are given a list of numbered choices, and are prompted to type in the number for the course of action you want to take. This game was developed by a professor at the real-life ELI in Newark, with a writing style intended for students learning English as a…

title: Clearer
description: Developed by HVB Software Platform DOS Published by HVB Software Released 1991 Genre Action Gameplay Paddle / Pong Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description The objective of Clearer is to clear the screen. The game ends after three rounds. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Eamon Adventure Disk 4 - Quest For Trezore
description: Eamon Adventure Disk 4 - Quest For Trezore Also For Apple II, Atari ST Published by PC-SIG Released 1988 Genre Role-Playing (RPG) Gameplay Interactive Fiction / Text Adventure, Puzzle elements Perspective Text-based / Spreadsheet Interface Text Parser Setting Fantasy, Medieval Description Eamon was one of the earliest role-playing games available for the Apple II. It was also perhaps the first ever adventure game construction set. The game was public domain, so it was mainly distributed in Apple user groups and by trading with friends. The main game consists of the Eamon Master disk, which has the Main Hall and a short adventure called the Beginner's Cave. You start the game in the Main Hall, where you create a new character or select an old character. You are able to buy weapons, spells, and armor and go on your adventure. title: Fluf!
description: Official Site Fluf! Platform DOS Published by RufusPro Software Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Fluf! is a maze-based action game which vaguely follows the same general idea as Pac-Man , with a few important differences. Most obviously, the maze layouts and the marauding monsters are different from level to level, and instead of gobbling up all the dots the goal is to flip the blue squares over to red (by simply walking over them). These factors notwithstanding, the baddies still roam the passages and would happily make a meal of our white fluffy protagonist should they meet. Echoing its inspiration, the game throws the occasional fruit bonus at the player, but instead of helpful power-pills or side tunnels there are deadly traps: the "black hole" tile will end the game immediately if encountered, no matter how many lives are left. One breed of nasties will occasionally turn red tiles back into blue, requiring more…

title: Molefest
description: Platforms DOS, Windows Released 2002 Genre Puzzle Perspective Top-down Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Molefest is a single player, freeware, variant of Pipe Mania but instead of laying pipes to carry water the player is laying a pathway so that the mole can find its way home. The player cannot progress from one level to another until the current level has been completed. The game has sound, three levels of difficulty, a high score table and is mouse controlled From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Paddle, The
description: Platform DOS Released 2002 Genre Action Gameplay Paddle / Pong Perspective Top-down Description The Paddle is a simple horizontal adaptation of the classic Pong . The game allows to compete with a computer or against a human player. Players control a paddle represented by a red or blue line. Paddles are on the opposite side of the screen, at the top and at the bottom. The game ends when one of the players cannot reflect the ball. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Tommy's ATC
description: Developed by Tommy's Toys Platform DOS Released 1986 Genre Simulation Description Tommy's ATC is a single player, shareware, air traffic control game. The player takes the role of the air traffic controller for the Greater Metropolitan Area of Podunk. In the centre of the game area is a cross representing runways 1 and 2. Aircraft appear in the window identified by a letter, their height and direction. The player enters commands to alter the heading, the height and so-on in order to bring planes into land or to guide other planes through take-off to an exit point. As with most of Tommy's games it uses character graphics and is entirely keyboard controlled. It has basic sound effects and command line switches to start the game with sound turned off and to force either a colour or monochrome display From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Transball
description: Developed by Brain Games Platform DOS Published by Brain Games Released 2003 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Transball is an action game, inspired by Thrust and Zarathrusta . The player controls a ship sent to recover the stolen energy spheres that provide all energy for future humanity. On each level, the player must reach the sphere, pick it up with his attractor beam, and carry it out of the level. The player's ship is subject to gravity and must be controlled by carefully firing off its thrusters to regulate the speed. The ship can be rotated freely to control the direction of thrust. Bumping into an obstacle destroys the ship and forces a restart of the level. Furthermore, the attractor beam only has a limited range and once the player has picked up the sphere, he must fly slowly enough to avoid leaving the sphere behind. Additionally the ship has a limited amount of fuel and once it runs out, the…

title: Turbo Blackjack
description: Platform DOS Released 1985 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Cards / Tiles, Casino / Gambling Perspective 3rd-person (Other) Description Turbo Blackjack is a shareware, keyboard controlled, card game for up to seven players. In this implementation of the game there is the option to play against computer opponents, such seats are occupied by an 'auto player'. The game's AI players follow guidelines laid down in the 1975 book "Green Felt Money: How to win at blackjack -- from beginning to end" All players start with $5000 and can bet any amount up to a table limit of $10000. The game plays like most standard blackjack games, players make their bets, get dealt two cards, the dealer turns one of their cards over and players can Hit, Stand, Split if appropriate etc. The game has several configuration options. The table rules, number of decks, dealer hits soft seventeen and others can be changed during the game. Other options such as adding / removing players, enabling/disabling sound and…

description: Developed by The Dennis Courtney Five Platform DOS Published by The Dennis Courtney Five Released Mar, 1997 Genre Role-Playing (RPG) Pacing Turn-based Perspective 1st-person Description Mazzembly 1997 receives an extra dimension in this extended tribute remake, which still stars aspiring demoscener Demulamu as he tours the "virtual reality demo party", trying to accumulate eliteness and fame on his path to scene g0dhood. His escapades now take the form of a 3D dungeon crawler, where the randomly-generated levels are experienced from a first-person view; climbing up the ranks will involve wandering around, interacting, finding/buying/using items, participating in party events, and/or resorting to violence (booze optional). title: Pitman
description: Official Site Pitman Developed by Tristar Platform DOS Published by Tristar Released Apr 28, 2004 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Platform Perspective Side view Interface Direct Control Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Pitman shares its general idea with an identically-named Game Boy title , although it isn't directly based on the latter. This puzzle platformer puts you in the shoes of a jovial stick figure prospecting for diamonds; your greedy little quest takes you through 22 different ANSI-styled levels. Each one is a puzzle unto itself, and your goal is to collect all the yellow diamonds by manipulating the environment to allow access - without getting trapped. Brown walls can be pushed and stacked on top of each other, blue walls disappear on touch, and diamonds are picked up by simply walking into them. However, such interaction is only possible when walking left or right: for instance, you cannot pick up a diamond (or dig through a blue wall) by landing on top of it, or by climbing…

title: Rockets
description: Developed by WelCom Systems Platform DOS Released 1986 Genre Action Gameplay Shooter Perspective Side view Visual 2D scrolling Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Rockets is a single-player, space based, shooter that is entirely keyboard controlled. The game starts by drawing a star-field on screen and populating it with a planet and asteroids. The planet is an obstacle that a spaceship cannot fly over but the asteroids are effectively just scenery. It then positions the player's ship and an enemy ship on screen and the object is to destroy as many enemy ships as possible before all ships are exhausted. As the player progresses the enemy ships become faster at tracking and firing. The game features destructible scenery, when a ship explodes near a planet, or asteroid, a chunk of that object is destroyed. It also has a speed up / slow down feature that allows it to be played on different systems. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Exploding Atoms
description: Platform DOS Published by InteReS Released Sep 07, 1992 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Real-Time Description Exploding Atoms is a two-player, shareware strategy game played between one person and the computer or two people. The game is played on an 8x8 grid. Players take turns placing atoms onto cells on the grid. Each cell has an associated value and when the cell holds that number of atoms it explodes sending atoms into neighbouring cells and if they now contain four atoms they too will explode and so on. Eventually the player's begin to compete for the same cells and as they advance into each other's territory the colour of the atoms in the cells changes. The winner is person who occupies all the squares at the end of the game. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Most Certainly Not Pool II
description: Most Certainly Not Pool II Platform DOS Published by Mooseware Development Released 1994 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description Most Certainly Not Pool II is not a pool game. It is a single-player game based around three balls on a sort of table but it is not a pool game. It is more of a time limited puzzle with balls than a pool game. In a rectangular play area are one red ball, one blue ball, one red hole, one blue hole and one greyish cue ball. The object is to knock the red ball into the red hole, the blue ball into the blue hole, or both balls into their respective holes using the cue ball. The cue ball is controlled by the arrow keys. The longer a key is held down then the faster it moves in a particular direction. Time is limited and to continue to the next level the task must be achieved before time runs out. Points are scored for potting a ball and a bonus is awarded for any time remaining on the clock, this turns into a penalty if the time has expired…

title: Notyet
description: Developed by Grog Productions Platform DOS Published by MVP Software Released 1996 Pacing Real-Time Perspective Top-down Genre Puzzle Interface Direct Control Gameplay Tile Matching Puzzle Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Notyet is a single player, shareware, keyboard controlled, tile matching puzzler. The game area consists of a series of concentric rings. In the centre of these rings is the players gun. The rings rotate and by shooting, and hitting, arrows on the surrounding rings the player can alter the direction in which they rotate. Also on the rings are coloured tiles in the form of trigrams, by shooting the tiles the player can push them to a ring that is further out. When two tiles of the same colour but on adjacent rings come together they disappear scoring points and giving the player's gun more energy. The objective of the game is to clear all tiles from the level so that the player can advance to the next, the full game has seventeen worlds. Obviously there are…

title: Zottris
description: Platform DOS Released 1992 Genre Puzzle Pacing Real-Time Gameplay Falling Block Puzzle Description Zottris is a single player, shareware, falling block game. Square blocks fall from the top of the screen to the bottom. When they hit the bottom of the screen the player can destroy them but they cannot be destroyed in flight. Destroying blocks costs the player Zot points which can only be replenished by generating a row of the same colour bricks which disappear and score the player points. As the player's point total increases they advance to another level, the gameplay remains the same but the background colour changes and the blocks appear and fall at a faster rate. The game ends when the bricks reach the top of the screen. The game has optional sound but has no save/load or high score functions. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Automon
description: Platform DOS Released 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Pacing Turn-based Perspective Top-down Gameplay Board Game Description Automon is a freeware monopoly game for up to eight players. While the rules are the same as the classic Parker Brothers Monopoly board game, this implementation has some novel features: Players can use any printable character as their game token. Games can be saved and restarted. Any or all players can be set to play automatically Common playing variations such as pre-dealing deeds, putting tax money on Free Parking, relaxing colour lot requirements, allowing re-rolls on leaving jail, disabling housing shortages etc. may be individually enabled. All aspects of the game may be edited at any time. Players can be added or subtracted, options changed, player order changed etc. The speed of the game (duration of delays, etc.) can also be set. title: Doublelink
description: Platform DOS Released Jan 19, 1991 Genre Puzzle Pacing Real-Time Gameplay Falling Block Puzzle Description DoubleLink is a single player, shareware, falling block game. In this game the falling blocks are bi-coloured capsules. The game area is populated with 'meanies', coloured frowning faces, and the objective is to clear these by making rows of four blocks of the same colour. This scores points and makes the blocks and any 'meanies' the row contains disappear. Note 1: Blocks only disappear in groups of four, if a longer string is formed then the surplus blocks will be left behind Note 2: diagonal rows do not count in this game. There are ten levels in this game, the harder the level the more 'meanies' are on screen at the start of the game. The game is entirely keyboard controlled. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: How-Two Build a Robot!
description: Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Description How-Two Build A Robot! is a single player, shareware, platform game in which the player must collect all the parts needed to build a robot and take them to the laboratory where they are assembled. Naturally there obstacles to over come, in this case there are gates lifts and barriers to navigate around, switches to switch, a stock control robot that takes components to its stock room, and the whole game must be completed before the supply of battery power runs out. The game is entirely keyboard controlled and has basic sound effects such as bleeps and whistles. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: Meteor Rescue
description: Developed by PLBM Games Platform DOS Published by PLBM Games Released 1996 Genre Action Pacing Real-Time Perspective 3rd-person (Other) Gameplay Shooter Setting Sci-Fi / Futuristic Description Meteor Rescue is a single player, keyboard controlled game that is very similar to Meteor Mission and may well be a later version of that game. Once again some poor astronauts pave been abandoned on a desolate planetoid. It's your job to swoop them up and bring them home. This is a game of two halves. In the first part the player's ship is held in a sort of cage in the drop ship which moves left /right across the top of the screen. As soon as the main engines start the floor of the cage retracts and the ship begins its descent. Timing here is important as the space between the drop ship and the landing pads below contains orbiting rocks which must be avoided. Once the ship has landed the astronaut beams aboard and the ship begins its ascent. The rate of ascent can be increased but not decreased…

title: DOS Quadraz
description: Official Site DOS Quadraz Developed by ASM Software Platform DOS Published by ASM Software Released 1996 Genre Puzzle Gameplay Cards / Tiles Perspective Top-down Interface Point and Select Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description This tile-flipping puzzle game is a forerunner to the author's later creation, Quadromania . The 10x10 game board is made up of tiles that can be cycled through 5 different states. Clicking a tile will also modify the eight neighboring tiles; cells on the edge of the board, which aren't surrounded by eight tiles, cannot be clicked. The board is jumbled by the computer, and the objective is to return it to its original state (all grey tiles) without taking too many moves. There are five difficulty levels, which determine how much vandalism is inflicted on the board at the start of the game - higher levels require more moves to solve. From Mobygames.com. title: Cbgtron
description: Platform DOS Released 1991 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Arcade Description Cbgtron is a shareware, two player game that is inspired by the light-cycle race in the film TRON . The players start in the centre of the game arena heading in different directions. As they drive around the arena they leave drive around the game area leaving a solid trail behind them. The object of the game is to cause other players to crash into one of these trails or the edge of the game area. The first player to win the required number of rounds, the default is ten, wins the game. In some matches the arena has solid walls while in others there are gateways this making it harder to trap an opponent. The game is entirely keyboard controlled, uses character graphics and has sound effects. Trouble is, you have a limited number of moves (or 'rounds') to carry out your escape: take too many turns, and you're out. title: Flyswat
description: Platform DOS Released Apr, 1983 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Side view Visual Fixed / Flip-screen Description Flyswat , as the descriptive title conveys, simulates an everyday activity that's decidedly less fun than what's usually associated with games: the annoyance of being pestered by a housefly while sitting in your easy chair and trying to read a book! Seeking to end the distraction, you pull out your trusty flyswat and attempt to flatten the buzzing little pain-in-the-butt. This is done by moving a cursor across the screen, getting within swatting distance of the fly, and hitting space to do the grisly deed; the difficulty level determines how fast and unpredictable the fly will get. When you finally splatter the pest, you'll be scored by the time and number of swats it took you. title: Great Canadian Scientists CD-ROM
description: Barry Shell created the GCS Research Society in 1993. At the time, people had nowhere to go to find out about the work and achievements of Canadian scientists. Working in his spare time and funded by government grants, Shell researched and interviewed dozens of Canadian scientists, and in 1995 he posted the profiles to a personal website at Simon Fraser University where he worked. That website led to the book Great Canadian Scientists and this companion CD-ROM featuring video interviews and science games. In 2001, the Society's science.ca website was born with funding from the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) PromoScience program. Since then, the site has received nearly 40 million unique visits, and now averages over 1 million unique visits per year and around 15 million hits per year. Another book, the award-winning Sensational Scientists: The Journeys and Discoveries of 24 Men and Women of Science was published in 2005, and is also based on the…

Navigating the town is super confusing, since all of the walls and doors look exactly the same, so it's very difficult to know where you're going. title: Proton
description: Developed by Clove Software Platform DOS Published by Clove Software Released 1987 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description Proton is a single-player computer adaptation of Photon , a.k.a. The player controls a single member of Blue Squad, while the computer controls the other two (and the entire Red Squad). Each team attempts to outscore the other within the time limit. You gain points by blasting the opposing team, and lose them if you get shot yourself (or worse, shoot your own teammates); this also disables your gun for a few seconds. After five successful shots at your opponents, you'll have to "recharge" by shooting the enemy base. When the time is up, the team with the higher cumulative score gets the match. From Mobygames.com. title: Frazzle!
description: Platform DOS Released Jul 12, 1990 Genre Strategy/Tactics Gameplay Board Game Description Frazzle! is a dice game for one, two or four players. In this game players take turns to roll the six dice. Points are scored for specific combinations based on how many dice of the same number have been rolled. At the end of each roll the player nominates a scoring dice and has the opportunity to re-roll. If they player re-rolls they must score with the remaining dice or else they are 'zonked' and no score is added to their total for that round. If a player succeeds in scoring with all six dice then they can continue their turn by re-rolling all of them. The objective of the game is to score more than ten thousand points which seems like a lot but fifteen of the thirty-six possible combinations scores over 1000 points. The game is entirely keyboard controlled and has a command line function for monochrome play. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

Each side makes one move per turn (moving a single piece to any adjoining square), and the objective is to eliminate the opponent's pieces. To do this, pieces may be captured by jumping over them (like checkers, but in any direction); or "infected" when the other side places its own piece in a neighboring square, which causes the victim's pieces to change their color to that of the infecting piece. However, each side does this differently - your blue pieces infect the four squares…

The SAM missiles home in on the player's 'copter but can be avoided by making continuous changes to course, speed and height. The 'copter can withstand three direct hits, after that the player has a 50/50 chance of surviving subsequent hits. The player's score is based on the number of tanks destroyed. The game is entirely keyboard controlled and as with most of Tommy's games it makes extensive use of the function keys. F9 for example fires the missiles while F3/F4 adjust the difficulty level. Other function keys change the size of the game area, adjust the sighting arrows, and so-on. It has basic sound effects and…

title: Tommy's Saucer

The story behind the game is that a space ship crash landed in Tommy's back garden and that after helping the aliens fix it Tommy was able to put together a mock-up of the ship which is now available for us to play with. The actual game consists of a window into which enemy alien ships occasionally appear. The player's task is to target them and shoot them down. Energy expended on ray beams and energy shields gradually automatically replenishes itself over time. As with most of Tommy's games it uses character graphics and is entirely keyboard controlled. It has basic sound effects and command line switches to start the game with sound turned off and to force either a colour or monochrome display. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

title: AxTrons
description: Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Perspective Top-down Description AxTrons is a trap-'em-up / arena survival game taking place in a randomly generated playfield. You, puny Earthling, are thrown onto the arena floor where ten slavering aliens await, with nothing but your wits and an assortment of traps to get you by. If you get out alive, you may be found worthy to join the InnerGalactic ParaGlomerate, whatever that is... but can you survive? You start each round with a limited amount of energy, which can be increased by collecting energy packets and Power Coins (spectators occasionally throw new coins onto the field). As the aliens attempt to hunt you down, you must dispatch them by laying down traps, barbs and grids - each type of device has a different tactical usage. You may also engage the enemies in melee combat, which mutually depletes your energy counts until the stronger one survives. Moving and dropping traps costs energy, too, so every little drop…

title: CleanUp
description: Platform DOS Released 1989 Genre Action Gameplay Arcade Description CleanUp is a single player, keyboard controlled, shareware puzzle game. It is a reworked version of a game 1979 game by Doug Schiller that was released on the TRS-80 . The game area consists of randomly scattered blocks among which are gold stars. The player must negotiate their way around this arena collecting the stars. The game is keyboard controlled, pressing a non-arrow key ends the game as does colliding with a block or crossing the player's previous pathway. The game is scored with the score calculation being based on the number of stars collected, the speed at which the game was being played, and the length of the path taken by the player. The game has a high score table and basic sound effects, bleeps and whistles. From Mobygames.com. Original Entry

This game is a Blackjack game which offers the following features: Play with up to 4 other players. Use up to six decks Changeable the game rules Game statistics Bats can be systematically increased as the count sweetens. In game card counting, plus a customised card counting option Customisable strategies plus the option to have the game verify their effectiveness by playing up to 30000 hands quickly The player can 'change their seat' at the table at any time. Statistics on other payers A replay feature for the last game Al AI players have their own biographies and styles From Mobygames.com. Original Entry
